jobs.title: Lead Learning Experience Designer
jobs.excerpt: The Wikimedia Foundation is seeking a Lead Learning Experience Designer to create innovative, engaging, and accessible learning experiences that strengthen the capacity of volunteers and communities across the Wikimedia movement.
jobs.description:
The Wikimedia Foundation is seeking a Lead Learning Experience Designer to create innovative, engaging, and accessible learning experiences that strengthen the capacity of volunteers and communities across the Wikimedia movement. You'll help contributors develop the confidence, skills, and knowledge they need to participate effectively, navigate Wikimedia’s communities and practices, and grow as contributors.

In this role, you'll partner with Foundation teams, affiliates, researchers, subject matter experts, and volunteers to understand learner needs, identify barriers to participation, and develop learning experiences that support contributors at different stages of their journey.

This role goes beyond traditional instructional design. You’ll think like a learning product designer, finding the right approach for each challenge, whether that means creating an online course on Wikimedia’s learning management system (LMS), WikiLearn, producing multimedia content, experimenting with emerging technologies, or embedding learning into existing experiences and workflows. You will do all this while ensuring the experiences you create are culturally responsive, accessible, and relevant to a global audience. This role is intended for an experienced individual who is comfortable operating with a high degree of autonomy and making decisions in complex, evolving environments.

Success in this role means being a curious, resourceful problem solver who understands how people learn, grow, and participate. You can think big about how learning can strengthen the Wikimedia movement, while also rolling up your sleeves to build, experiment, and iterate on solutions that make a meaningful difference.

Responsibilities

  • Design and develop innovative digital learning experiences, capacity-strengthening resources, and performance support solutions for contributors across the Wikimedia movement.
  • Partner with product teams, community groups, researchers, and subject matter experts to identify learning needs, contributor challenges, and opportunities to strengthen participation.
  • Determine the right learning approach for each opportunity, whether that be a self-paced course, video, interactive experience, AI-enabled support, workshop, or embedded guidance.
  • Develop learning experiences that support contributors in understanding new tools, workflows, policies, governance processes, and community practices across Wikimedia projects.
  • Rapidly prototype, test and iterate on learning experiences, using modern authoring tools, multimedia, and AI tools.
  • Apply learning science, user-centered design, and learning experience design methodologies to create engaging, effective, and inclusive solutions.
  • Evaluate learning effectiveness using learner feedback, participation data, and other qualitative and quantitative insights, continuously improving content based on evidence and community feedback.
  • Contribute to the ongoing evolution of the Foundation's learning strategy by staying current with learning technology, online learning, AI, and digital engagement, identifying opportunities to expand and strengthen learning offerings across the movement.
  • Ensure learning resources reflect Wikimedia's values of openness, collaboration, equity, and knowledge sharing.

Qualifications

Required

  • Experience designing and developing digital learning experiences for diverse, global audiences.
  • Demonstrated experience creating engaging e-learning, instructor-led, virtual, or blended learning solutions.
  • Experience using a learning management system (LMS) to develop, organize, and publish learning content.
  • Demonstrated ability to diagnose capability gaps, identify the right interventions, and rapidly design, build and improve learning experiences.
  • Excellent written communication and content development skills, with the ability to simplify complex concepts for diverse audiences.
  • Experience collaborating with cross-functional stakeholders and subject matter experts.
  • Commitment to accessibility, inclusive design, and culturally responsive learning practices.

Preferred

  • Experience working with volunteer communities, open knowledge initiatives, nonprofits, or international organizations.
  • Experience designing learning for multilingual audiences and collaborating across cultures and time zones.
  • Experience creating learning in modern digital environments using tools such as Rise, Storyline, Camtasia, Adobe Creative Suite, Figma, video editing tools, AI content generation platforms, or similar technologies.
  • Experience partnering with product teams or using product design approaches, such as user research, experimentation, prototyping and iteration.
  • Knowledge of experimentation methods, A/B testing, learning analytics, product analytics, and continuous improvement practices.
  • Familiarity with Wikimedia projects, the Wikimedia movement, or open-source communities.

You'll Thrive in This Role If You...

  • Think like a designer and builder, comfortable moving from identifying challenges to creating, testing and improving solutions.
  • Are curious about how people learn, what motivates participation, and how to leverage modern methods and technology to create memorable learning experiences.
  • Are energized by ambiguity and enjoy figuring out what needs to be built rather than waiting for a predefined assignment.
  • Excel at collaborating with people from different backgrounds, languages, and areas of expertise.
  • Balance creativity with evidence and structure, using data, research, and feedback to guide decisions.
  • Care deeply about accessibility, inclusion, and creating learning that supports equitable participation.
  • Are inspired by Wikimedia's mission to make knowledge freely available to everyone.

About the Wikimedia Foundation

The Wikimedia Foundation is the nonprofit organization that operates Wikipedia and the other Wikimedia free knowledge projects. Our vision is a world in which every single human can freely share in the sum of all knowledge. We believe that everyone has the potential to contribute something to our shared knowledge, and that everyone should be able to access that knowledge freely. We host Wikipedia and the Wikimedia projects, build software experiences for reading, contributing, and sharing Wikimedia content, support the volunteer communities and partners who make Wikimedia possible, and advocate for policies that enable Wikimedia and free knowledge to thrive.

The Wikimedia Foundation is a charitable, not-for-profit organization that relies on donations. We receive donations from millions of individuals around the world, with an average donation of about $15. We also receive donations through institutional grants and gifts. The Wikimedia Foundation is a United States 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization with offices in San Francisco, California, USA.

As an equal opportunity employer, the Wikimedia Foundation values having a diverse workforce and continuously strives to maintain an inclusive and equitable workplace. We encourage people with a diverse range of backgrounds to apply. We do not discriminate against any person based upon their race, traits historically associated with race, religion, color, national origin, sex, pregnancy or related medical conditions, parental status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, or any other legally protected characteristics.

The Wikimedia Foundation is a remote-first organization with staff members including contractors based 40+ countries*. Salaries at the Wikimedia Foundation are set in a way that is competitive, equitable, and consistent with our values and culture. The anticipated annual pay range of this position for applicants based within the United States is US$117,437 to US$177,624 with multiple individualized factors, including cost of living in the location, being the determinants of the offered pay. For applicants located outside of the US, the pay range will be adjusted to the country of hire. We neither ask for nor take into consideration the salary history of applicants. The compensation for a successful applicant will be based on their skills, experience and location.

*Please note that we are currently able to hire in the following:
US States: Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, District of Columbia*, Florida, Georgia, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Puerto Rico*, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, West Virginia, Wisconsin and Wyoming (*US Territory or Federal District)

Countries: Brazil, Canada, Colombia, France, Germany, Ghana, India, Indonesia, Italy, Kenya*, Mexico, Morocco, Netherlands, Poland, Singapore*, South Africa, Spain, Switzerland and the United Kingdom. Our non-US employees are hired through a local third party Employer of Record (EOR) and must have current work authorization in their location. (*citizens/permanent residents only)

We periodically review this list to streamline to ensure alignment with our hiring requirements.

All applicants can reach out to their recruiter to understand more about the specific pay range for their location during the interview process.

If you are a qualified applicant requiring assistance or an accommodation to complete any step of the application process due to a disability, you may contact us at or +1 (415) 839-6885.

Why Portugal

So, now we are looking for our Engineering Managers to join us in Portugal.

About the role

As an Engineering Manager, you will drive the successful delivery and execution of projects within your teams. You will manage end-to-end technical planning, ensuring that product requirements are translated into actionable tasks, while orchestrating collaboration between various stakeholders, including engineers, product managers, QA, and UX. This role requires a deep understanding of software design and development and the ability to plan, execute, and deliver product features in a timely and predictable manner. You will also be responsible for maintaining high technical standards, managing team bandwidth, and ensuring project milestones are met with efficiency and accuracy.

What you’ll get to do

  • Own end-to-end delivery and execution across cross-functional teams within your product area, ensuring predictable and high-quality outcomes.
  • Evaluate business and product requirements for technical feasibility and architectural alignment, translating them into well-defined EPICs and technical user stories.
  • Partner closely with Product Managers, UX Designers, and Engineers to continuously refine, groom, and prioritize the backlog.
  • Plan and drive sprint execution with clearly defined goals, using project planning tools to establish timelines, delivery milestones, and surface dependencies early.
  • Champion engineering processes and rituals that enable strong collaboration, accountability, and team efficiency.
  • Monitor team velocity and capacity to optimize resource allocation, proactively balancing bandwidth against delivery commitments.
  • Coordinate cross-team dependencies and stakeholder alignment to remove bottlenecks and maintain smooth execution.
  • Stay hands-on in critical initiatives by guiding design decisions, enforcing sound design patterns, and participating in code reviews to maintain high engineering quality.
  • Ensure robust monitoring, alerting, and observability for all owned services, consistently meeting defined SLIs and SLOs.
  • Partner with Product Managers to define, track, and publish post-release product metrics, driving transparency and continuous improvement.

To succeed in this role, you should have

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field.
  • 8-10 years of experience as a Software Developer, Software Engineer, or in a similar hands-on technical role.
  • 5+ years of strong experience building production systems using Java and Spring Boot.
  • Minimum 3 years of proven engineering leadership experience managing high-performing teams.
  • Solid grasp of Agile methodologies, including sprint planning, backlog grooming, and iterative delivery.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate complex product requirements into well-structured EPICs, user stories, and tasks.
  • Strong backend engineering expertise; exposure to frontend technologies is a plus.
  • Experience with project planning and tracking tools to visualize and manage delivery timelines.
  • Familiarity with engineering, product health metrics, and monitoring tools to drive data-informed decisions.
  • Hands-on capability to debug complex production issues, lead incident response, and conduct blameless RCA.
  • Good understanding of modern deployment practices, including CI/CD pipelines, release management, and associated metrics.
  • Ability to drive alignment across cross-functional stakeholders, both technical and non-technical.
  • Excellent risk management, dependency tracking, and stakeholder communication skills.
  • Proven track record of improving team velocity, delivery predictability, and engineering excellence.

Generic Skills

  • Problem-solving: Ability to assess complex problems, find solutions, and make sound decisions.
  • Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills, including technical documentation and stakeholder reporting.
  • Adaptability: Able to thrive in a fast-paced, changing environment, adjusting strategies as needed.
  • Attention to Detail: Meticulous in documenting technical requirements and ensuring all aspects of a project are accounted for.

Supervisory skills

  • Team Management: Experience in managing and mentoring engineers, ensuring team growth and performance.
  • Resource Allocation: Ability to assess bandwidth and manage resource distribution to optimize team performance.
  • Feedback: Conduct regular performance reviews, providing constructive feedback and fostering a growth-oriented environment.
  • Stakeholder Management: Lead project status reviews, manage expectations, and ensure smooth communication between teams and leadership.

What we can offer you

  • Culture - We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. We’ve built a company where all opinions carry weight and where all voices are heard. We value and respect each other and always look out for one another. Above all, we are human.

jobs.excerpt: WHO WE ARE: Headquartered in Southern California, Skechers—the Comfort Technology Company®—has spent over 30 years helping men, women, and kids everywhere look and feel good.
jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE:
Headquartered in Southern California, Skechers—the Comfort Technology Company®—has spent over 30 years helping men, women, and kids everywhere look and feel good. Comfort innovation is at the core of everything we do, driving the development of stylish, high-quality products at a great value. From our diverse footwear collections to our expanding range of apparel and accessories, Skechers is a complete lifestyle brand.

ABOUT THE ROLE:
The Sr. Manager, Identity Security & Access Management (IAM) at Skechers is a key member of our global information security team who will work as a subject matter expert, trusted partner, and ambassador to help protect Skechers critical customer facing and core business applications. This role leads the identity security program responsible for policy, architecture direction, governance, roadmap, and identity risk reduction across workforce, privileged, non-human, and AI agent identities. We are looking for someone who will continue growing and maturing a practice that is focused equally on enablement as well as assurance, who will apply a technology first approach to providing seamless secure authentication and the frameworks necessary to enable humans, machines, and agents to operate securely at scale.

Skechers' increasingly AI enabled hybrid technology environment requires an individual who is well versed in traditional and modern applications, cloud infrastructure, automation, and identity platforms, and who is comfortable operating in an advisory or hands on leadership role as the situation demands. This role partners closely with IT infrastructure and operations teams that administer identity providers and access processes, helping define standards and engineer solutions that can be adopted across the enterprise. The candidate who will find the most success and fulfillment brings a genuine interest and passion for information security, a love for learning, a positive attitude, and a desire to roll up their sleeves and dive into the deep end.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Lead the team responsible for identity security and access management at Skechers, including IAM engineering, governance, and architecture.
  • Own IAM program strategy, roadmap, priorities, budget planning, metrics, and reporting.
  • Establish and maintain IAM policies, security standards, reference architectures, and best practice guidelines for workforce, privileged, non-human, and AI agent identities.
  • Provide direction and support for the adoption and management of phishing resistant authentication, passkeys, risk-based authentication, PAM, and just in time services.
  • Lead identity governance and administration strategy, including access review frameworks, evidence automation, remediation tracking, and control maturity.
  • Develop and mature governance for non-human identities, including service accounts, API keys, bots, automation accounts, workload identities, and AI agents.
  • Guide identity risk reduction and posture management across traditional systems, SaaS, cloud, and modern application infrastructure.
  • Develop, build, and maintain technology patterns, integrations, and automation frameworks that enable contextual authentication, authorization, and scalable access governance.
  • Partner with IT Infrastructure and IT Operations teams that administer platforms such as Okta, Active Directory, Azure AD / Entra ID to define requirements, provide technical guidance, and support adoption.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders across technical and business functions to develop and maintain the roadmap for enterprise identity security solutions, including privileged access, identity governance, machine identity, and cloud entitlement management capabilities.
  • Oversee IAM technology vendors, implementation planning, product roadmap alignment, support escalation, and service quality.
  • Maintain up-to-date knowledge of IAM and identity security best practices, including Zero Trust Architecture, non-human identity management, AI agent governance, and cloud identity risk.
  • Stay up to date and informed on changing IT and information security trends.
  • Create, communicate, and continuously monitor and improve metrics and KPIs.
  • Collaborate effectively with diverse internal teams to help drive security maturity.
  • Contribute positively to the culture of information security across the org.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Excellent understanding of authentication, authorization, role-based access, attribute-based access, least privilege, segregation of duties, entitlement management, and identity lifecycle concepts.
  • Proven experience leading a practice around identities, access, accounts, authentication, authorization, entitlements, permissions, privileged access, and non-human identities.
  • Positive track record developing IAM strategy, standards, architecture patterns, and implementation roadmaps in a large enterprise environment.
  • Experience with identity platforms and capabilities such as Active Directory, Azure AD / Entra ID, Okta, LDAP, IGA, PAM, SSO, MFA, risk-based authentication, and passkeys.
  • Experience with IAM governance, user access review frameworks, control design, evidence automation, compliance partnership, and remediation tracking.
  • Working understanding of identity security risk, posture management, cloud entitlement management, Zero Trust concepts, and governance for machine identities and AI agents.
  • Ability to partner with infrastructure, operations, application, cloud, and business teams where identity operations are owned outside the information security team.
  • Ability to manage program roadmaps, budget input, technology evaluations, vendor relationships, implementation oversight, and stakeholder expectations.
  • Ability to communicate issues effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills.
  • Strong work ethic with attention to detail.
  • Ability to excel in a fast paced and rapidly changing environment.

REQUIREMENTS:

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required.

  • 7+ years of experience with identity and access management, cybersecurity, infrastructure, cloud, or security architecture.
  • 5+ years of experience with multiple authentication and authorization solutions, directory platforms, identity governance, privileged access, or related identity security technologies.
  • 3+ years of management or team leadership experience.
  • Proven ability to mentor, grow, and develop a team.
  • Experience managing technology vendors, implementation planning, and product roadmaps.

The pay range for this position is $175,000-$205,000/yr USD.

Skechers, a global Fortune 500® company, develops and markets a diverse range of lifestyle and performance footwear, apparel, and accessories. Serving over 180 countries and territories, Skechers connects customers to products through department and specialty stores, e-commerce and digital stores, and through our more than 5,300 Skechers retail locations.

As a trusted C-Suite / executive level advisor on ServiceNow offerings, the Principal Customer Success Executive (PCSE) owns the post-sale customer relationship, aiming to increase customer satisfaction and drive retention through Impact delivery. Principal CSEs are experienced individuals who bring a consultative, problem-solving approach to partnering with senior customer stakeholders to derive value from our platforms. This role drives business transformation by maximizing the long-term strategic value of ServiceNow and ensuring that every aspect of the customer’s platform and capability are ready for expansion.

They provide strategic direction and mentorship to both customers and ServiceNow teams managing complex, multi-workstream programs. They play a pivotal role in resolving escalations and mitigating risks, ensuring adoption and usage is maintained at healthy levels. Principal CSEs focus on ensuring the customer recognizes the value of the ServiceNow Platform at all levels and stages, facilitating a smooth path to both renewal and up- and cross-sell.

Overall, Principal CSEs are responsible for fostering the relationship with C-suite level stakeholders in a smaller number of strategically important Impact accounts, with the aim of increasing customer satisfaction and driving retention and upgrades, where applicable.

Job Responsibilities

Lead high-complexity transformations in our largest and most strategic customers, ensuring all ServiceNow Customer Excellence roles align and deliver in accordance with governance frameworks, customer objectives, and organizational priorities; ultimately chaperoning Impact value management and demonstrating strategic oversight.

Proactively identify professional services pipeline opportunities through product capabilities road mapping, value blueprints and adoption analysis, providing pre-sales support for funnel opportunities as requested.

Partner with Impact team members (e.g., Customer Success Managers) leveraging the joint visibility of customer insights to create executive-ready narratives.

Work with senior executives to shape and influence customer organizational strategy by identifying emerging trends, refining best practices, and aligning delivery approaches with evolving market demands, and providing industry-specific thought leadership.

Drive operational consistency and excellence by standardizing delivery methodologies and ensuring adherence to governance and quality standards, interfacing with Delivery as required.

Establish relationships with ServiceNow leaders, advocating for product evolution based on customer insights, and mentoring other Customer Success resources on transformation best practices.

Identify areas of risk and take steps to prevent customer or revenue churn.

Work closely with Sales Teams to define and execute product adoption and customer retention plans.

Provide prescriptive guidance on internal project/program governance and help the customer create the appropriate governance models and ensure adherence.

Help the customer identify incidents where contractual SLAs were missed and take necessary action.

Improve overall customer satisfaction, as well as the satisfaction of their internal customers.

Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI's potential impact on the function or industry.

Significant experience collaborating with senior IT and business leaders, with a track record of successfully translating corporate strategy/objectives with the applied use of ServiceNow technology in the context of the client’s environment.

Minimum 15+ years in client-facing roles with a focus on account management, consulting, or transformation leadership. Experience in executive-level leadership roles, with a proven track record of influencing senior stakeholders and driving strategic outcomes, is strongly preferred.

IT Strategy and Planning

Human Resources

IT Processes

IT Governance

IT Portfolio, Program and Project Management

IT Project Delivery (SDLC)

Under the leadership of the National Director, Play, this self-starting individual is responsible for stewarding and driving fundraising success for the Play program through the recruitment, development, and stewardship of content creators and streamers who fundraise for Breakthrough T1D. The National Manager champions a strategic and integrated approach within the Play program, including streamer recruitment and onboarding, event and campaign support, community management across Twitch and Discord, and content creator engagement that increases fundraising participation and revenue at all levels. This role also ensures an extraordinary creator and community experience while assuring accuracy in data reporting practices and adherence to national standards of program delivery. The National Manager provides expertise and leadership to help ensure initiatives are positioned and supported for revenue growth through resource development including budget and event planning, data analysis, communication, and training. The collective body of work delivers successful implementation and financial results of the program to fulfill Breakthrough T1D's mission.


Key Responsibilities:


Fundraising

  • Collaborates with the National Director, Play and key stakeholders to develop and deliver core Play program strategies and best practices, through Game Over, T1D!, Pokethon, Raid for Research, T1.Done, Creators for Cures, and other Play campaigns and events, to ensure revenue and awareness results are achieved.
  • Cultivates and stewards relationships with current and past fundraisers, top creators, and industry contacts to drive retention and year-over-year growth in participation and revenue.

Volunteerism

  • Partners with streamers and creators to build strategies that encourage them to activate their own networks, sub-communities, and co-streamers, and to solicit funding and support from their audiences and industry contacts where they have influence.
  • Builds, establishes, and maintains a reliable pipeline of prospective streamers and community volunteers for each Play campaign and event; supports succession planning to sustain participation year over year.
  • Coaches streamers, partners and volunteers by applying best practices from across Breakthrough T1D’s national peer-to-peer (P2P) fundraising programs; actively seeks out learnings from other internal and external P2P programs.
  • Helps manage Play's Discord server, supporting and coordinating volunteers who help foster a welcoming, active community for streamers, gamers, and supporters.

Awareness

  • Builds a collaborative relationship with Marcom, Community Engagement & Strategic Initiatives, and Program Resources stakeholders to elevate and enhance opportunities to increase awareness, engagement, and revenue.

  • Shares Play community stories and successes through social media, blog posts, and email communications.
  • Reviews trends and works with the National Director and department stakeholders to address areas of opportunity as it relates to diverse audience recruitment and engagement.

Semafor is a global news platform for an increasingly complex world in which consumers are overwhelmed by too many news sources and unsure what to trust. We are building Semafor to enable world-class journalists to deliver reporting and insights with rigor in journalistic forms that ensure a new level of transparency. As a global platform, Semafor recognizes that smart people can disagree and that informed readers need to understand alternative points of view from competing centers of power and culture in a multi-polar world. Want to join us? Read on.

About this Role

Semafor is seeking an experienced Contract Audience Developer to support audience development and event execution for Semafor World Economy, our flagship global convening in Washington, D.C.

This role will take end-to-end responsibility for audience development across assigned events and programming, from initial audience strategy and list building through invitations, registration, attendee communications, and on-site readiness.

The successful candidate will combine strong audience judgment with hands-on operational capabilities, ensuring that each event attracts the right mix of attendees, meets its participation targets, and delivers a seamless attendee experience.

Audience Strategy & Curation

  • Translate event briefs into clear audience criteria, including seniority, industry, organizational relevance, and desired audience composition.
  • Work with internal stakeholders to align audience recruitment with editorial priorities, event objectives, and partner commitments where applicable.

Audience Acquisition & Communications

  • Draft compelling invitation copy, registration messaging, reminders, and other attendee communications.
  • Coordinate with the design team on the development and deployment of event invitations and associated creative assets.
  • Manage invitation distribution, personalized outreach, follow-ups, and attendee communications.
  • Track audience acquisition performance and proactively adjust outreach strategies to meet targets.

Event Website & Registration Management

  • Manage event website content, registration pages, and RSVP workflows for assigned events.
  • Ensure all event information, registration details, speaker content, and attendee-facing materials are accurate and current.
  • Maintain accurate registration data and manage attendee status changes, cancellations, and waitlists.
  • Coordinate with relevant teams to troubleshoot registration issues and ensure a seamless attendee experience.

Capacity & Audience Management

  • Own RSVP tracking and audience reporting for assigned events.
  • Manage registration pipelines against venue capacity, attendance projections, and audience composition targets.
  • Monitor not only the volume of registrations but also the quality and relevance of confirmed attendees against the event brief.
  • Identify audience gaps and proactively recruit additional participants to maintain the desired balance.

Cross-Functional Event Delivery

  • Work closely with Editorial, Events, Design, Partnerships, and Audience Development teams throughout the event lifecycle.
  • Maintain clear internal reporting on audience recruitment, registration progress, and operational readiness.
  • Prepare final attendee lists, event briefings, and handoff materials for on-site teams.
  • Support event execution, attendee management, and post-event reporting as required.

Ideal Experience & Skills

  • Strong experience in audience development, event marketing, or attendee acquisition for high-profile business events.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage event audience development from initial planning through execution.
  • Excellent judgment in curating senior executive and business audiences.
  • Strong copywriting skills, with experience developing professional event invitations and communications.
  • Proficiency with CRM systems, event registration platforms, spreadsheets, and website content management tools.
  • Ability to manage registration pipelines, capacity targets, and multiple simultaneous deadlines.
  • Highly organized, resourceful, and comfortable taking ownership in a fast-paced environment.
  • Experience working across editorial, commercial, marketing, and event operations teams.

Additional Job Details

This position is ideally based out of either our New York, NY or Washington, D.C. offices, but we are open to remote candidates outside either region.

Compensation; Flat weekly rate of $1,800.

jobs.excerpt: Job Type: Full-Time l Location: Texas l Department:Data Center Delivery l Reporting to: Vice President, Data Center Delivery | Work Location Type: #remote IREN is a vertically integrated AI Cloud provider, delivering large-scale data centers and GPU clusters for AI training and inference.
jobs.description:
Job Type: Full-Time l Location: Texas l Department:Data Center Delivery l Reporting to: Vice President, Data Center Delivery | Work Location Type: #remote

IREN is a vertically integrated AI Cloud provider, delivering large-scale data centers and GPU clusters for AI training and inference. IREN’s platform is underpinned by its expansive portfolio of grid-connected land and power in renewable-rich regions across North America, Europe and APAC.

Reporting to the VP, Delivery, the Director, Network Deliveryis the single point of accountability for the delivery of telecommunications, network infrastructure, fiber and supporting technology systems across every IREN data center campus – on campus, and the off-campus carrier and service-provider routes that serve each campus. The Director ensures that network infrastructure is designed correctly, constructed correctly, documented correctly and operationally ready when each building and campus is turned over, and that this happens the same way on every campus.

The Director builds and leads the Network Delivery team: Senior Project Managers – Network Delivery assigned to each campus, and the Project Managers supporting them. The Director sets the network delivery standards, templates and acceptance criteria that those teams deliver to; owns the portfolio-level schedule, budget and risk picture for network delivery; and manages the strategic relationships with carriers, service providers, telecommunications contractors and network equipment vendors so that each campus benefits from the leverage, pricing and lessons of the whole portfolio.

With 100% renewable energy, we build, own and operate our data centers and take pride in being at the forefront of sustainable solutions for the ever-evolving applications of high-performance compute. We believe that human progress is invaluable, but it should be done in the right way – responsibly, sustainably and having a positive impact on the communities we operate in.

Responsibilities

Strategy and standards
  • Set the network delivery strategy for the portfolio: contracting model for telecommunications scope, carrier and service-provider strategy, standard designs and long-lead equipment approach, in alignment with Network Engineering, Sourcing and the VP, Delivery.
  • Define, publish and maintain network delivery standards – carrier entrance and diversity requirements, MMR and MDF/IDF standards, pathway and structured cabling specifications, labeling and naming conventions, testing and acceptance criteria – and ensure they are incorporated into campus design templates and construction documents.
  • Own the DCIM/NetBox data standard: what is captured, by whom, in what format and at what stage of construction, so that every campus is handed over with an accurate infrastructure record from day one.
  • Drive continuous improvement: lessons learned from each campus are captured, standards are updated and the next campus is delivered better.
Team leadership
  • Build, lead and develop the Network Delivery team: hire and assign Senior Project Managers – Network Delivery to campuses, set clear and stretch expectations, give regular feedback, manage performance and build a pipeline of network delivery talent against campus demand.
  • Set delivery priorities and resourcing across campuses; resolve workload allocation and staffing with campus Project Directors and the VP, Delivery.
  • Ensure all personnel, including contractors, under the team’s management are inducted and trained in line with company requirements; role-model a positive HSE culture and drive for zero harm.
Portfolio delivery and governance
  • Own the portfolio network delivery schedule and ensure network milestones – carrier service turn-up, MMR ready-for-service, backbone and building network readiness – are integrated into each campus master schedule and never delay building commissioning or handover.
  • Own the network delivery budget across campuses; work with project controls to maintain cost plans, forecasts and contingency; advise early of cost impacts and communicate variances to the VP, Delivery.
  • Run the network delivery governance cadence: campus-level reviews with each Senior Project Manager – Network Delivery, a consolidated portfolio review for the VP, Delivery, and the consistent, concise reporting senior leadership relies on.
  • Maintain the portfolio risk register for network delivery; lead risk assessments on new campuses during development and front-end engineering so that carrier access, diverse routing and entrance requirements are secured before site layout is fixed.
  • Approve contract awards and change orders for network scope within delegated authority; support negotiation of major carrier, service-provider and vendor agreements.
Carrier, service-provider and vendor management
  • Own the strategic relationships with carriers, service providers, telecommunications contractors and network equipment vendors; establish master agreements, standard pricing and service levels that each campus can draw on.
  • Set measurable performance KPIs for carriers, contractors and vendors across the portfolio; run periodic performance reviews and act on underperformance.
  • Serve as the escalation point for carrier, service-provider and vendor disputes and for off-campus route and entrance issues; engage utilities, landowners and local government where required.
  • Work with Development and Network Engineering on carrier access and connectivity due diligence for prospective campuses, and on commitments made to customers and Operations on service availability.
Integration with campus delivery and engineering
  • Partner with campus Project Directors so that network scope is planned, sequenced, resourced and reported as an integral part of every campus and building, with dependencies on civil, electrical, mechanical and building trades identified and managed.
  • Partner with Network Engineering so that logical design, VLANs, IP addressing and equipment standards are reflected in delivery standards and in construction documents before construction.
  • Coordinate the network dependencies of operational technology systems – BMS, EPMS, fire and life-safety monitoring, security, CCTV, access control, Wi-Fi and environmental monitoring – with the functions that own those systems.
  • Lead the handover of network infrastructure to Operations on each campus against an agreed acceptance standard; ensure as-builts, test results, labeling and DCIM/NetBox records are complete and validated.
Communications and executive reporting
  • Provide the VP, Delivery and the executive team with concise, reliable, consistent reporting on network delivery status, risks, schedule and budget across all campuses; escalate incidents, issues and concerns as required, with a recommendation.
  • Represent Network Delivery with senior stakeholders inside and outside IREN – executive leadership, carriers and service providers, strategic partners and customers – with credibility and composure.
  • Collaborate closely with Project Delivery, Network Engineering, Operations, Sourcing and Development leadership with a team-first, project-first mentality.

Requirements

  • Minimum 12 years of telecommunications, network infrastructure or data center industry experience.
  • 5+ years of proven project management and people leadership delivering telecommunications or network infrastructure on mid to large data center or mission-critical programs of similar complexity to IREN’s, including having led network delivery for a full campus or multi-building program.
  • Demonstrated experience building and leading a team of project managers and managing performance across multiple concurrent projects or sites.
  • Qualifications in an engineering, telecommunications or related discipline, or demonstrable experience and technical knowledge in data center network and fiber infrastructure; master’s degree or MBA preferred.
  • Deep technical expertise in outside-plant and inside-plant fiber, carrier and MMR delivery, campus backbone and data center structured cabling and network infrastructure.
  • Proven track record establishing and managing carrier, service-provider and vendor relationships and agreements, including negotiation and dispute resolution.
  • Executive presence and reporting: proven ability to document and communicate program risks, schedule and budget clearly and consistently to executive leadership, in writing and in person.
  • Experience in a fast-paced growth environment and in solving complex problems with company-wide impact.
  • OSHA 30.
  • Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Suite (Project, Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint).
Preferred qualifications – network and telecommunications
  • Outside-plant fiber and carrier delivery: long-haul and metro routes, right-of-way and permitting dependencies, diverse entrances, splicing and OTDR acceptance, carrier POP and handoff coordination, service orders and turn-up.
  • Inside-plant and campus backbone: MMR design and fit-out, MDF/IDF, pathways and cable tray, structured cabling (fiber and copper), cross-connects, patch panels and labeling standards.
  • High-capacity network services: 100G/400G connectivity, DWDM/optical transport, and coordination with Network Engineering on logical design, VLANs and IP addressing.
  • Operational technology networks: network dependencies for BMS, EPMS, fire and life-safety monitoring, security, CCTV, access control, Wi-Fi and environmental monitoring.
  • Infrastructure records: NetBox or other DCIM platforms, asset and connectivity documentation, naming conventions and as-built validation.
  • Standards and program governance: authoring and rolling out design and delivery standards, templates and acceptance criteria across multiple sites.
Also highly regarded
  • Experience on direct-to-subcontractor (multi-prime) delivery as well as GC-led delivery.
  • PM certification (PMP or equivalent) highly regarded but not required; tertiary qualifications in project management desirable.
  • Industry credentials such as BICSI RCDD or DCDC, Cisco or equivalent networking certifications, or fiber-optic technician certifications (e.g. FOA CFOT).
  • Familiarity with SAP and with scheduling tools such as Primavera P6.
  • Flexible approach to work hours across time zones; frequent travel to campuses.
Other important requirements
  • A clear criminal record check is required.
  • Must provide own steel-toed work boots; all other PPE is supplied.
  • Must be based at or within reasonable reach of an IREN campus, or have plans to relocate before starting work; frequent travel across campuses is required.
  • IREN operates across multiple countries and time zones; a flexible approach to work hours is required, with travel to other IREN sites as needed.

Benefits

Compensation
  • Actual compensation will be determined based on factors such as experience, qualifications, and market data for the region.
  • Total Compensation package may be inclusive of annual incentive bonus, equity (long-term incentive).
  • Relocation (as appliable and based on successful candidate circumstances)
Health & Wellness
  • 100% company paidhealth insurance premiums(medical, dental, and vision)for employees, 75% company paid coverage for dependents
  • Company-paid short-term and long-term disability insurance
  • Voluntary life, critical illness, and accident coverage available
  • Health Savings Accounts (HSA) – when combined with the High Deductible Health Plan
  • Employee Assistance Program and wellness resources
Retirement & Financial Wealth
  • 401(k) retirement plan with company match
  • Access to financial planning and legal services
Time Off & Leave Programs
  • Paid Time Off (PTO) and paid holidays
Growth & Development
  • Internal skills training and advancement pathways
  • Professional development to support certifications, continuing education, or role related training
Community & Culture
  • Company events and team-building activities
We value diverse perspectives and believe that skills can be developed. If you’re passionate about this role, we want to hear from you — whether you meet every criteria or not. Your unique experiences might be exactly what we need!

Job title: Medical Science Liaison Rhinology - Southeast

  • Location: Remote, US

About the job


The Medical Science Liaison (MSL) is a field-facing role that serves as a trusted scientific partner to key external experts, conducting frequent scientific exchanges to enhance understanding of Sanofi's products. The MSL executes stakeholder engagement plans to gather insights that inform medical strategies and future research, while staying current on therapeutic developments to identify research opportunities and support evidence generation.


This role involves recognizing and sharing insights about patient and healthcare provider needs, maintaining effective communication with internal stakeholders across Medical Affairs and Commercial Operations, and ensuring full compliance with company, industry, legal, and regulatory requirements through excellent governance and risk management.


Join the engine of Sanofi’s mission — where deep immunoscience meets bold, AI-powered research. In R&D, you’ll drive breakthroughs that could turn the impossible into possible for millions.

About Sanofi:


We’re an R&D-driven, AI-powered biopharma company committed to improving people’s lives and delivering compelling growth. Our deep understanding of the immune system – and innovative pipeline – enables us to invent medicines and vaccines that treat and protect millions of people around the world and are supported and enhanced through our diverse portfolio of medical device and diagnostic products. Together, we chase the miracles of science to improve people’s lives.


Main Responsibilities:


1. Scientific Engagement: Conduct one-on-one and group interactions with Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs) and healthcare stakeholders, sharing medical/scientific information about products and disease management within regulatory guidelines.

2. Stakeholder Mapping & Strategy: Identify, profile, and prioritize ~50 stakeholders using the Scientific Engagement Model; develop territory and individual engagement plans aligned with Medical Affairs strategy.

3. Relationship Building: Establish long-term peer relationships with KOLs, payers, and HCPs by demonstrating strong clinical knowledge and articulating the medical value of Sanofi products.

4. Congress & Event Presence: Attend scientific congresses, symposia, and organize educational meetings or advisory boards to establish Sanofi's medical presence in the field.

5. Medical Information Support: Respond to unsolicited requests for medical information on products and disease states; support speaker training for continued scientific education.

6. Insight Generation: Gather feedback from stakeholder interactions, critically evaluate published studies, and report insights that inform Sanofi's medical strategies, messages, and product development.

7. Internal Collaboration: Share scientific information and external insights with Medical Affairs, Commercial Operations, Regulatory, and other internal teams while ensuring compliance with company and regulatory policies.

8. Evidence Generation Support: Identify clinical trial sites, monitor disease epidemiology, support protocol development, and facilitate investigator-sponsored study (ISS) submissions through approved processes.

9. Healthcare Policy Awareness: Understand healthcare policies, guidelines, and clinical practices at local, state, and national levels as they relate to the therapeutic area.

10. Independent Operation & Compliance: Work remotely with minimal supervision, travel nationally/internationally as needed, and maintain strict regulatory boundaries between non-promotional medical activities and commercial operations.

About you

Basic Qualifications

  • Advanced degree in a technical, scientific or medical field (MD, PhD, Pharm D preferred) or other Relevant Life Science degree (RN/MS/PA/NP)
  • Must reside in territory. This position will cover the West territory— currently including Florida, Alabama, Georgia, Mississippi, Louisiana, Tennessee, and South Carolina (subject to change). Candidate must live within the territory near a major airport with flight availably to adequately cover the territory and necessary travel.
  • Minimum of 2 years of experience in pharmaceutical industry, Medical Science Liaison role, or relevant clinical practice. Additional years of experience are an asset. MSL experience strongly preferred.
  • Candidates with relevant Immunology clinical experience consisting of Rhinology, Otolaryngology and/or Allergy may be considered.
  • Clear understanding of medical practice, clinical decision making, and healthcare systems related to patient care.
  • Ability to interpret key scientific data and translate this information to meet educational and research needs.
  • Demonstrated ability to address educational and research needs through delivery of cutting edge scientific/evidenced based data.
  • Understand the design and execution of research studies.
  • Exemplary communication and presentation skills.
  • Experience in working on multi-disciplinary teams and managing significant volume of projects.
  • Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record and ability to pass a complete background check.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Actively listens to others and is adept at confidently stating expert opinion while respecting the positions of others - can exert diplomacy while standing firm on a position.
  • Utilizes effective, professional communications to cultivate strong working relationships with internal and external colleagues, flexible in own approach to people and situations.
  • Skillfully plans, prioritizes, and executes multiple responsibilities and projects.
  • Demonstrates effective leadership skills (by example and through accomplishments), steps forward to handle challenges within scope of authority.
  • Deep understanding and knowledge of local regulations and codes of practice for pharmaceutical industry, in particular as they apply to the non-promotional activities of this role.
  • Demonstrates scientific expertise - stays abreast of data, treatment trends, and new information in the profession and ability to articulate therapeutic knowledge and translate expert feedback into appropriate insights.
  • Knowledge of relevant healthcare systems, the evolving medical landscape, regulatory and payer environment, public health and industry trends.
  • Proficiency in digital tools.

Why choose us?

  • Bring the miracles of science to life alongside a supportive, future-focused team.
  • Discover endless opportunities to grow your talent and drive your career, whether it’s through a promotion or lateral move, at home or internationally.
  • Enjoy a thoughtful, well-crafted rewards package that recognizes your contribution and amplifies your impact.
  • Take good care of yourself and your family, with a wide range of health and wellbeing benefits including high-quality healthcare, prevention and wellness programs and at least 14 weeks’ gender-neutral parental leave.
  • Be part of a pioneering biopharma company that engages patients early in drug development and uses their insights to design studies that reflect real-world needs.
  • Help improve the lives of millions of people globally by making drug development quicker and more effective.
  • Work at the forefront of drug discovery, harnessing cutting-edge AI, data, and digital platforms to push the boundaries of science.

Devenez chauffeur indépendant avec DriiveMe Partenaire

Accédez à des missions rémunérées de convoyage de véhicules partout en France, avec une organisation flexible et des frais de route pris en charge.

👉 Inscrivez-vous ici pour accéder aux missions :

DriiveMe est la plateforme leader européen du convoyage de véhicules. Chaque mois, plus de 20 000 missions rémunérées sont proposées à notre communauté de chauffeurs et convoyeurs indépendants partout en France.

Les grands acteurs de l’automobile font confiance à DriiveMe pour déplacer leurs véhicules : Stellantis, Aramisauto, Ayvens, Tesla, Volkswagen, Hertz, Avis, Europcar, et bien d’autres.

Partout en France, des centaines de sociétés ont besoin de déplacer des véhicules d’un point A à un point B. Elles publient chaque jour leurs besoins sur DriiveMe afin de proposer ces missions à la communauté DriiveMe Partenaire.

En quoi consiste une mission DriiveMe ?

C’est simple : en tant que chauffeur indépendant, vous conduisez un véhicule d’un point A vers un point B. Voici comment ça fonctionne :

  1. Vous créez votre compte sur

  2. Vous accédez aux missions disponibles dans votre région.

  3. Vous consultez le trajet, la rémunération et les conditions de chaque mission.

  4. Vous réservez en quelques clics les missions que vous souhaitez réaliser.

  5. Le jour de la mission, vous récupérez le véhicule au point de départ et le livrez au point d’arrivée.

  6. Une fois la mission terminée et validée, vous recevez votre paiement automatiquement sous 10 jours.

Pourquoi devenir chauffeur indépendant avec DriiveMe Partenaire ?

  • Complément de revenus : chaque mission est rémunérée, avec un prix connu à l’avance.

  • Organisation flexible : vous choisissez librement les missions que vous souhaitez effectuer.

  • Frais de route pris en charge : carburant et péages sont remboursés selon les conditions de la mission.

  • Plateforme simple et intuitive : consultation, réservation et suivi des missions en ligne.

  • Missions partout en France : de nouvelles opportunités sont publiées chaque jour.

Combien suis-je rémunéré ?

Votre chiffre d'affaires dépend du nombre de missions que vous choisissez de réaliser.

Chaque mission dispose d’une rémunération spécifique, définie selon le trajet, le nombre de kilomètres et la complexité du transport.

Avant de réserver une mission, vous connaissez les informations essentielles : lieu de départ, lieu d’arrivée, rémunération et conditions de prise en charge. Vous êtes libre de réserver uniquement les missions qui vous conviennent.

Profil recherché

Pour rejoindre DriiveMe Partenaire, vous devez idéalement :

  • disposer d’un permis B valide ;

  • être indépendant ou prêt à le devenir ;

  • être sérieux, ponctuel et rigoureux ;

  • respecter les procédures de prise en charge et de livraison des véhicules ;

  • être disponible pour réaliser des missions ponctuelles dans votre région ou ailleurs en France.

We’re a team of friends bound together by a mission to preserve our planet for future generations through innovative energy solutions and modern infrastructure. Intersect develops, constructs, and operates the most ambitious power and data center infrastructure in the country by co-locating industrial demand with dedicated gas and renewable power generation.

Intersect was acquired by Google in March 2026 and operates as an independent subsidiary. We are developing and constructing multiple gigawatts of energy and data center projects in the U.S., enabling more data center and generation capacity to come online faster. We’re on an aggressive growth trajectory and looking for people hungry to tackle the largest energy challenges on the planet.

Location & Team Gatherings

Intersect has been a fully flexible workplace since its founding in 2016. We’ve been very intentional about the way we do things. We are not work-from-home, hybrid, or in-office - we are any and all of those options! Deepening social connections and offering shared experiences is a cornerstone of the way we work. We connect as a team at our Team Week experiences four times a year and at our recently established Hub locations - SF Bay Area, NYC Metro Area, NY; Denver, CO; Austin, TX; Calgary, AB; and Toronto, ON.

We are currently looking for candidates located within 60 miles of any of the listed hubs to foster more in-person connections while maintaining our flexible remote culture.

About this role

As a Campus Project Director on Intersect's Construction team, you'll oversee the complete execution and delivery of multi-facility clean energy campuses designed to power Google data centers. You will lead complex, multi-technology buildouts encompassing utility-scale solar, wind, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and high-voltage substation and transmission infrastructure, serving as the single point of accountability for site performance, vendor integration, and executive reporting.

You will collaborate closely with internal engineering, procurement, asset management, and executive leadership, as well as external EPC partners and hyperscale client stakeholders. By deploying modern construction management platforms and leveraging clear, strategic communication, you'll drive operational excellence while ensuring safety and quality standards across all sites.

Team overview

This team plays a critical role in advancing Intersect's mission to accelerate the clean energy transition. The Construction team partners across development, engineering, procurement, and operations to build resilient, gigawatt-scale power infrastructure that energizes critical digital infrastructure. Joining this team means directing high-impact energy campuses from earthworks to commercial operation, shaping how clean energy powers the future of computing while growing alongside a dedicated group of industry leaders.

What you'll do

Direct Multi-Technology Campus Execution

  • Lead end-to-end site delivery for multi-facility energy campuses combining solar, wind, BESS, and high-voltage transmission scope.

  • Manage and mentor Campus Project Managers, serving as their primary escalation point and holding overall accountability for the success of the campus as a whole.

  • Establish site governance, schedule baselines, and budget oversight across simultaneous project builds powering Google data center infrastructure.

  • Incorporate advanced field management tools, including Terabase Construct and AI Clearing, to track site progress, optimize craft sequencing, and ensure quality.

Drive High-Voltage Integration and Technical Compliance

  • Oversee the seamless integration of high-voltage substations, interconnection facilities, and generation assets into active grid and off-grid interconnections.

  • Troubleshoot complex engineering, procurement, and field bottlenecks alongside technical experts to maintain strict commercial operation timelines.

  • Evaluate natural gas power integration options where applicable to enhance campus resilience and microgrid performance.

Lead Executive Communication and Strategic Stakeholder Alignment

  • Synthesize high-density technical, financial, and schedule data into executive-ready slide decks for leadership and key off-taker stakeholders.

  • Deliver regular strategic briefings to executive leadership detailing campus health, risk contingencies, and critical path milestones.

  • Maintain strong working relationships with EPC firms, key equipment vendors, utilities, and local regulatory authorities.

Strengthen Safety, Cost, and Operational Culture

  • Enforce rigorous safety programs across all campus sites, cultivating an environment that prioritizes total personnel well-being.

  • Manage financial workflows using Stampli and internal financial tools to control capital expenditure, change orders, and contract compliance.

  • Utilize generative AI platforms such as Claude and Gemini to streamline reporting workflows, executive briefing prep, and team documentation.

What you'll bring

  • Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Civil/Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline.

  • 10+ years of project management experience in power generation, with 3+ years specifically as a Project Director leading utility-scale clean energy projects.

  • Proven track record delivering complex campus-scale builds featuring solar, wind, BESS, and high-voltage (HV) scope; natural gas experience is a plus.

  • Demonstrated ability to synthesize complex technical challenges and produce executive-level presentation decks for C-suite leadership and external client stakeholders.

  • Proficiency with modern construction, workflow, and AI tools including Terabase Construct, AI Clearing, Stampli, Lucidchart, G Suite, Claude, and Gemini.

  • Willingness to travel up to 50% to active campus sites with a minimum once-a-month onsite footprint.

  • Strong team builder and strategic thinker with an adaptable leadership style focused on cross-functional alignment and field enablement.

  • Deep commitment to long-term value, safety, and authentic leadership, fully aligned with Intersect's core values: Equity, Humility, Authenticity, Long-run Value, and People Come First.

Total Rewards

Total Compensation: $221,000 - $260,000 (total compensation includes base salary + bonus in USD)

Equity: Beyond your salary, you’ll receive an Equity Grant, giving you a meaningful stake in our parent company.

Health & wellness: 100% premium coverage for you and your dependents on medical, dental, and vision

Time to recharge: Unlimited PTO, plus two company-wide breaks (Fourth of July & end of year)

Family support: Up to 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, plus 6 additional weeks for birth parents; access to family planning and family care support through Carrot and Maven

Mental health: Free access to Spring Health, including 5 free therapy and psychiatry sessions, plus a Headspace account for mindfulness and meditation through our physical health vendor, Wellhub+

Perks & extras: $150 monthly food stipend, $150 monthly reimbursement for cell phone and internet, pet insurance allowance, full home office setup, free access to UrbanSitter with $625 in quarterly company-paid credits, ActiveHero, and One Medical

jobs.excerpt: About the Job:As a Senior Full Stack Engineer on LaunchDarkly’s AgentControl team, you'll build critical systems such as the web application that customers interact with on a daily basis and distributed systems that power AI evaluations at scale.
jobs.description:
About the Job:

As a Senior Full Stack Engineer on LaunchDarkly’s AgentControl team, you'll build critical systems such as the web application that customers interact with on a daily basis and distributed systems that power AI evaluations at scale. These systems enable customers to control, monitor, and optimize their agent’s functionality.

LaunchDarkly’s AgentControl team is on a mission to manage the complete software development lifecycle for shipping agents to production, from configuring to benchmarking to observing and beyond. AgentControl enables teams to adjust agent behavior without needing a redeploy or code change, while also running experiments, monitoring agents in production, and putting guardrails around AI as usage scales. The product spans offline evals, real-time observability, prompt and workflow optimization, and decision-making around quality, accuracy, relevance, and cost. The AgentControl team has a huge opportunity ahead of it; it's a strategic bet for LaunchDarkly, and we need your help writing the next chapter in our story.

Responsibilities:

  • Build and maintain scalable backend services, distributed systems, and APIs that power the AgentControl product
  • You’ll primarily work in Go, Python, and TypeScript and will work directly with other technologies and tools such as AWS, CockroachDB, Datadog, DeepEval, and FastAPI.
  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders, including product managers, designers, and other LaunchDarkly engineering teams, to understand real-world challenges and improve GenAI workflows using our own platform.
  • Keep up to date with the latest developments in the AI field and in software development best practices
  • Continuously optimize the performance, reliability, and scalability of our systems
  • Drive architecture and design discussions, offering thoughtful input and collaborating with peer engineers to identify trade-offs and make well-informed decisions
  • Take ownership of code in production, participate in on-call rotations, and help improve the reliability and maintainability of our systems over time.
  • Support teammates through thoughtful design reviews, knowledge sharing, and informal mentorship.

Qualifications:

  • 7+ years of professional software engineering experience, with a track record of shipping production-quality full-stack features.
  • Understanding of prompt engineering, fine-tuning models, or deploying AI services in production environments.
  • Experience with designing, implementing, and maintaining RESTful APIs
  • Experience writing production-ready code with emphasis on quality and maintainability
  • Experience with distributed systems or data ingestion
  • Strong computer science fundamentals
  • Committed to working in a communicative, collaborative environment
  • Comfortable navigating ambiguous challenges in a rapidly evolving domain, and excited about staying at the forefront of AI advancements
  • Strong sense of ownership and accountability for delivering impactful solutions
  • Proven ability to work closely with Product and Design teams to define requirements for new features in a fast-paced iterative environment
  • Bonus: Hands-on experience building GenAI features, Agents, and/or working with Large Language Models (LLMs), either through direct model integration or leveraging AI APIs like OpenAI, Google Cloud AI, or AWS Bedrock.

Pay:

Target pay ranges based on Geographic Zones* for Level 4:

  • Zone 1: San Francisco/Bay Area or NYC Metropolitan Area, Boston, Seattle - $187,000 - $257,000**
  • Zone 2: Irvine, LA, Monterey, Santa Barbara, Santa Rosa, Austin, Portland, Philadelphia, Chicago - $168,000 - $231,000**
  • Zone 3: All other US locations - $158,000 - $218,000**

LaunchDarkly operates from a place of high trust and transparency; we are happy to state the pay range for our open roles to best align with your needs. Exact compensation may vary based on skills, experience, and location.

*Within the United States, our geographic pay zones are defined by counties surrounding major metropolitan areas.
**Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), health, vision, and dental insurance, and mental health benefits in addition to salary.

About LaunchDarkly:

Modern software delivery was supposed to be the foundation for a thriving digital business but reality has proven otherwise. Slow, inefficient development cycles, costly outages, and fragmented customer experiences are preventing developers from building their best software. The LaunchDarkly platform helps developers innovate on new features faster while protecting them with a safety valve to instantly rewind when things go wrong. Developers can target product experiences to any customer segment and maximize the business impact of every feature. And by gradually rolling out new application components, they escape nightmare "big-bang" technology migrations.

The LaunchDarkly platform was built to guide engineers to the next frontier of DevOps by:

  • Improving the velocity and stability of software releases, without the fear of end customer outages
  • Delivering targeted experiences by easily personalizing features to customer cohorts
  • Maximizing the business impact of every feature through the ability to experiment and optimize
  • Coordinating the release and optimization of software to provide consistent experiences across mobile platforms and device types
  • Improving the effectiveness and productivity of engineering teams, by providing insights into engineering cadence and stability

At LaunchDarkly, we believe in the power of teams. We're building a team that is humble, open, collaborative, respectful and kind. We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.
