Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

Engineering at Qualified


Engineering at Qualified is a high-ownership, high-velocity environment where engineers ship customer-facing product to real enterprises at scale. We're building at the frontier of AI + product: developing agentic software and

embedding AI directly into our platform, using modern toolchains and processes that help engineers move faster while staying focused on high-impact problem solving.


Following our acquisition by Salesforce, we continue to operate with the pace and ownership of a startup, backed by the distribution, resources, and long-term runway of a global enterprise. Engineers have true end-to-end ownership from idea to production: scoping, implementation, testing, deployment, monitoring, and iterative improvement based on real customer feedback.


You'll work alongside a high-talent-density team that cares deeply about craft, performance, reliability, and user experience, and that raises the bar through collaboration, code review, and strong engineering principles. You'll make architecture decisions, solve meaningful system design challenges, and see your work land quickly with customers, without layers of approvals slowing you down.


The Role


As an Engineer on the AI Core team, you'll operate as a technical leader who turns ambiguous, high-stakes AI problems into durable, high-quality systems, while raising the technical bar for the broader team. AI Core builds the retrieval systems and agent infrastructure that power how our AI agents find, trust, and use knowledge, and the developer tooling that lets engineers across the company ship production agents quickly and safely.


You'll lead significant initiatives end to end: faithful answering over a customer's own knowledge, retrieval that combines RAG and hybrid search, content lifecycle controls such as freshness, deduplication and source precedence, transcript processing, and the frameworks, registries, and evaluation tooling that make building a production agent a paved path. You'll partner closely with product, design, and engineering leadership to decide what we build, how we build it, and how we measure whether answers actually got better.


What You'll Do


Lead retrieval initiatives end to end: Design, build, and operate retrieval systems using RAG and hybrid search (lexical plus vector, reranking, filtering) so agents answer from the right content with the right amount of context. Own delivery from scope and design through launch, monitoring, and iteration.


Build developer tooling for production agents: Drive technical design for the frameworks and platform pieces our engineers use to build agents, including multi-agent orchestration, shared primitives for prompts, tools, tracing, and evaluation.


Own answer quality: Diagnose why answers are thin, wrong, or inconsistent by separating retrieval problems from generation problems (prompt, token budget, model choice). Set a quality bar we can test against, and lead the

work to reach it.


Design content and data models: Define how content from documents,

knowledge bases, and call transcripts is ingested, segmented, labeled, and retrieved, including the primitives behind freshness, dedupe, source

precedence, and internal versus external visibility.


Make AI changes safe to ship: Build evaluation, observability, and rollout

practices (offline evals, online monitoring, regression detection) so we can change prompts, models, and retrieval with confidence. Evaluate multiple

solution paths and know when to trust, redirect, or override model and agent output.


Set performance and scaling benchmarks across the platform we own:


Define and track targets for retrieval and indexing, LLM provider usage, and agent orchestration.


Own operational health: Ensure the reliability and performance of the systems your team owns. Participate in on-call, lead incident resolution for your area, and communicate clearly with the team and stakeholders during incidents.


Use agentic development to raise leverage: Use coding agents by default for implementation, testing, refactoring, and documentation while holding a high validation bar. Create reusable workflows, patterns, and tooling that raise the effectiveness of your team beyond your own output.


Partner across functions: Work with product, design, and engineering

leadership to shape roadmap, tradeoffs, and requirements, and to translate strategy into concrete execution plans.


Raise team effectiveness: Mentor engineers, give high-quality code review and technical guidance, and improve standards, tooling, and processes.


Who You Are


Proven experience shipping production AI or backend systems in a high ownership environment, with a recent focus on LLM-powered applications.


Expertise building retrieval systems using RAG and hybrid search, including chunking and indexing strategy, embeddings, vector and lexical search,

reranking, and measuring retrieval quality.


Expertise building developer tooling that lets developers build production agents, which can include frameworks for multi-agent orchestration, an agent and tool registry, and shared infrastructure for tracing and evaluation.

Experience owning platform initiatives from design through adoption,

across systems such as retrieval and indexing, LLM provider integrations, and agent orchestration, including driving adoption and evolving the platform as usage grows.


Demonstrated technical leadership: you lead significant projects, design solutions for non-trivial problems by weighing tradeoffs, and influence architecture and execution beyond your immediate workstream.


Strong track record delivering complex projects with multiple stakeholders, dependencies, or phases.


Strong backend engineering fundamentals and proficiency in languages such as Ruby on Rails, Python, JavaScript, or Go, with SQL and RDBMS experience (PostgreSQL preferred).


Hands-on experience with the AI application lifecycle: experiment setup, dataset curation, offline evaluation, error analysis, deployment, and online evaluation.


Comfortable operating in ambiguity and driving clarity: you can frame problems, propose solutions, and align others.


Strong communicator across functions, able to explain technical ideas to both technical and non-technical audiences and to translate complex concepts into business impact.


Ownership mindset and bias for action. You raise the bar for the team through mentoring, code review, and your own work.


Curious and continuously learning, with an agent-forward approach to how you build software.


Nice to Have


Experience with pgvector or other vector indexes, and with query performance at scale.


Experience with content ingestion from third-party systems (document stores, knowledge bases, CRM knowledge objects) and the lifecycle problems that follow: sync state, dedupe, source conflict.


Experience processing conversation or call transcripts, including handling PII and consent constraints.


Experience designing evaluation suites that score qualities such as thoroughness and faithfulness, not only correctness.


Experience with voice or real-time conversational agents.


Experience with enterprise SaaS (especially B2B marketing or sales tech) or Salesforce/CRM integrations.


Startup experience and rapid shipping.


Why Join Qualified


Foundational impact: Shape how our AI agents retrieve, reason, and answer, and the tooling every engineer here uses to build them.


Lead real initiatives: Own significant projects end to end, with scope and

influence that grow as you deliver. You'll own the platform as it scales, from retrieval to model providers to agent orchestration, and set the performance and reliability bar that grows with the company.


AI as a core product surface: Turn new AI capabilities into dependable

experiences that customers trust, with strong engineering around evaluation, observability, and iteration.


High bar, low bureaucracy: Work with a team that values craft and decisive execution, where strong ideas win and shipping is the default.


Room to grow: Take on larger technical and product scope over time: leading projects, influencing architecture, and leveling up quickly.


If you're excited to build retrieval systems and agent infrastructure at the intersection of AI and enterprise software, we'd love to hear from you.


Unleash Your Potential

When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance andbe your best, and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you cando your best. Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.

About the Role

The role of Pharmacist Care Manager is a critical role at Fuze Rx. In this role, you will be responsible for ensuring the compliant, efficient, safe, and scalable operations for the Contact Center and Clinical Operations. A chief objective will be to establish operational excellence, particularly as it pertains to patient experience, employee morale, industry standards, compliance, and performance metrics. You will use your in-depth knowledge of Pharmacy regulations, clinical judgment, and patient safety practices to meet and exceed service level agreements. As a Care Manager, you will also work cross-functionally to develop new processes and programs that are key to Fuze Rx's success, and establish a culture of continuous improvement. You will supervise and develop your team and be responsible for employee engagement, training and communicating and adhering to performance standards.

The Data Governance Specialist supports the implementation and ongoing maturity of the enterprise data governance program within a federated operating model. The role partners with business data owners, stewards, and technology teams to establish consistent governance practices, strengthen data ownership and accountability, improve metadata and data quality, and support compliance with privacy, retention, and risk requirements. By coordinating governance activities, facilitating stakeholder engagement, monitoring performance, and promoting adoption of enterprise standards and tools, this role helps ensure data is well-managed, trusted, discoverable, and used responsibly across the organization

Some of the things you will be doing:

Data Governance Program Support

  • Support the implementation and maturation of the enterprise data governance framework.

  • Assist in developing and maintaining data governance policies, standards, procedures, and operating models.

  • Facilitate governance councils, stewardship forums, working groups, and governance-related meetings.

  • Track governance initiatives, decisions, action items, risks, and issue remediation activities.

  • Promote governance awareness and adoption across business and technology teams.

Data Ownership and Stewardship Enablement

  • Partner with business unit leads to identify and document Data Owners and Business Data Stewards.

  • Facilitate stewardship onboarding and training activities.

  • Clarify governance roles, responsibilities, decision rights, and accountability expectations.

  • Coordinate stewardship activities across data domains and business functions.

  • Escalate unresolved ownership, accountability, and stewardship issues through appropriate governance channels.

Metadata and Data Catalog Governance

  • Support the development and maintenance of business glossaries, data dictionaries, and governance metadata.

  • Establish metadata standards, governance workflows, and quality expectations.

  • Coordinate metadata collection and validation activities performed by business and technical stakeholders.

  • Monitor metadata completeness and governance compliance.

  • Promote effective use of enterprise data catalog capabilities.

Data Quality Governance

  • Support implementation of enterprise data quality policies, standards, metrics, and controls.

  • Facilitate identification, prioritization, and escalation of data quality issues.

  • Coordinate remediation efforts with business stewards, system owners, and technology teams.

  • Track data quality trends, root causes, and corrective actions.

  • Report on data quality performance and governance outcomes.

Policy, Compliance, and Risk Management

  • Support alignment of activities with regulatory, privacy, records retention, and risk management requirements. Support implementation of data classification, retention, and protection requirements.

  • Assist with governance assessments, audits, and compliance reviews.

  • Maintain governance documentation and evidence required for internal and external audits.

Stakeholder Engagement and Change Management

  • Collaborate with business, technology, analytics, security, privacy, legal, compliance, and risk stakeholders.

Hello. We’re Teya.

Teya was founded on a simple belief: local businesses deserve better.

They are the cafés, restaurants, salons, shops and entrepreneurs that bring character to our high streets, create jobs and keep communities moving. Yet for too long, financial services has made life harder for them - with clunky tools, poor support and complexity that gets in the way of running a business.

Teya exists to change that.

We’re building a financial platform for local businesses across Europe - one built around simple tools, thoughtful design and real human support. Our Members rely on us to help them run their business with confidence, and that responsibility shapes the way we work.

Company Overview

Robots & Pencils is an applied AI engineering firm building the next frontier of business architecture. We design and ship AI co-workers that integrate into enterprise operations and deliver measurable results for our clients. We're all in on AWS, combining deep UX capability with senior engineering talent to get AI into production fast and keep it there.
We’ve earned the trust of leaders across Consumer Products and Retail, Education, Energy, Financial Services, Healthcare, and Manufacturing and more, and earned a reputation as the nimble alternative to traditional global systems integrators. Founded in 2009, with delivery centers in Canada, the United States, Eastern Europe, and Latin America, we are smaller, faster, and more senior by design. Our teams average 15+ years of experience. We move fast, sweat the details, and build things that actually ship.

Position Overview

We’re looking for a Senior AI Engineer to design, build, and deliver production AI/ML systems. This role is ideal for an engineer with several years of experience who can confidently own features end-to-end, contribute to architectural decisions, and bring strong technical judgment to the problems they take on.

In this role, you will work as a key contributor on a cross-functional team, designing and implementing models, building the data pipelines and training workflows around them, and deploying systems to production environments. You’ll be joining real, in-flight work where reliability, performance, and scalability matter. You’ll collaborate with experienced engineers to enhance existing systems, deliver new capabilities, and contribute to the technical decisions that shape how our AI work scales over time.

Why This Role Matters

At Robots & Pencils, we design AI systems for a human world. Our name says it all. Robots and pencils means engineering paired with creativity, because every agent we ship has to work for real people in real workflows. That balance is baked into how we operate.

Every role here contributes directly to that mission. Here, you shape how AI systems integrate into enterprise operations, how teams move at real velocity, and how products create measurable impact for clients and the people they serve. We ship production-ready AI in 30 to 45 days. That pace demands people who take ownership, lead with craft, and care deeply about what they put their name on.

What You’ll Do

Craft & Delivery

  • Design, implement, and deploy ML/AI models end-to-end, from concept through production, including data pipelines, training workflows, and optimization for performance, accuracy, and efficiency
  • Maintain and evolve AI systems in production, monitoring for drift, debugging issues, and driving ongoing improvements to reliability and scalability
  • Bring an AI-forward coding mindset to your daily work, using tools like Claude and Cursor to ship higher-quality work at pace

Collaboration & Communication

  • Partner closely with product, engineering, and data teams to align AI work with broader product and business goals
  • Translate technical tradeoffs, model behavior, and constraints into terms non-specialists can act on
  • Participate actively in code reviews and design discussions, raising concerns and offering constructive feedback

Leadership & Influence

  • Contribute to AI architecture decisions with thoughtful perspective on tradeoffs and long-term implications
  • Take ownership of meaningful work end-to-end, including the unglamorous parts of getting AI into production
  • Raise the bar on engineering practices through your own work and by supporting more junior engineers when opportunities arise

What You’ll Bring

  • 4+ years professional software engineering experience, with 2+ years focused on AI/ML systems in production and hands-on experience with generative AI development
  • Strong software engineering background (Python or similar)
  • Working knowledge of cloud platforms, preferably with in-depth understanding of AWS services and AWS GenAI offerings
  • Proven ability to design and ship agentic systems
  • Experience with AI frameworks and orchestration tools
  • Experience with evaluation frameworks, and observability tools for LLM apps
  • Understanding of AI safety, responsible AI principles, prompt injection defenses, and PII handling
  • Hands-on experience building RAG pipelines: chunking strategies, embedding models, vector databases
  • API development experience, including designing and integrating with internal and third-party services
  • Cost optimization expertise: token economics, caching strategies, model routing, quantization
  • Working knowledge of Docker and Kubernetes for containerized deployments
  • Demonstrable, day-to-day usage and knowledge of AI-forward coding tools such as Claude Code and Cursor
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to navigate ambiguous technical challenges with sound judgment

You’ll Do Well Here if You Are

  • A doer. You see something broken and fix it. You'd rather move on clarity than wait for certainty.
  • A fast learner who knows you don't know everything. The AI landscape changes weekly. You're senior enough to know better and curious enough to keep learning anyway.
  • Direct in a way that makes the work better. You give honest feedback. You'd rather have the hard conversation than blow smoke.
  • Obsessed with craft. You know genius is in the details. You ship exceptional, not perfect, and you don't put your name on work you wouldn't stand behind.
  • Built for ownership. You honor commitments, admit mistakes fast, and back your teammates when a decision costs something. No handoffs, no finger-pointing.
  • All in. You treat clients' businesses like your own. You take the work seriously without taking yourself seriously.
  • Resourceful when the budget, timeline, or team is tight. Constraints don't slow you down. They sharpen you.
  • Glad to be in the room with people who care as much as you do. Our teams average fifteen-plus years of experience. We hire people who push each other to do better work.

Why Join Robots & Pencils?

At Robots & Pencils, we build intelligent systems for real-world environments, blending creativity, engineering excellence, and applied AI to help organizations work smarter.     • Participate in growth efforts as requested

    • Ensure all contractual deliverables are met/exceeded to the customer's satisfaction

    Education and Years of Experience: Bachelor's degree in computer science, information systems, engineering, cybersecurity, or a related field (or equivalent) with 8+ years of relevant experience, or a Master's degree with 6+ years of relevant experience.

    • Strong experience developing modern frontend applications using JavaScript, TypeScript, and Vue or comparable frontend frameworks

Kikoff: The Fintech Powering Financial Security at Scale
Kikoff is a profitable, pre-IPO fintech company on a mission to empower everyone to achieve financial security. With record revenue growth in 2025 and a unicorn valuation, we've built a suite of products that help millions of people build credit, access liquidity, and save money.
We're scaling fast. Join us if you want to build something meaningful and help millions of people move forward financially.

Why Kikoff:

We value extreme ownership, clear communication, a strong sense of craftsmanship, and the desire to create lasting work and work relationships. Yes, you can build an exciting business AND have real-life real-customer impact.

The Role

Kikoff is seeking its first government affairs leader to shape and advance the company's public policy agenda at the federal and state levels. You will be Kikoff's primary voice with legislators, regulators, trade associations, consumer advocates, and other stakeholders, and you will lead strategy to support a clear, workable legal framework for earned wage access (EWA). This is a high-impact, hands-on role for someone who builds durable relationships, translates policy into business strategy, and is comfortable operating in a fast-moving, evolving regulatory landscape.

The role will involve regular nationwide travel.

What You'll Do

  • Develop and execute Kikoff's government affairs strategy, with an initial focus on federal and state policy affecting earned wage access and consumer credit-building products.
  • Represent Kikoff before legislators, legislative staff, federal and state financial regulators, attorneys general, and other public officials.
  • Serve as Kikoff's representative to relevant trade associations and industry coalitions, taking active roles on committees and working groups and helping shape industry positions.
  • Build and maintain constructive relationships with consumer advocacy groups, community organizations, think tanks, and other stakeholders, including those who may hold differing views.
  • Monitor, analyze, and report on legislative and regulatory developments; assess business impact and recommend responses, including testimony, comment letters, and model legislative language, in coordination with Legal and Compliance.
  • Identify, hire, and manage outside lobbyists and consultants across priority states and at the federal level, including setting objectives, overseeing budgets, and evaluating performance.

  • Partner with Legal, Compliance, Product, and Executive teams to ensure policy strategy aligns with business priorities and product roadmaps.

  • Represent Kikoff at hearings, conferences, industry events, and stakeholder meetings nationwide.

  • 4–10 years of experience in government affairs, public policy, legislative or regulatory affairs, or advocacy, gained in-house, at a trade association, at a public affairs firm, or in government service.

  • Demonstrated track record of building and leveraging relationships with policymakers, regulators, and stakeholders at the state and/or federal level.

  • Experience engaging, directing, and managing outside lobbyists or consultants.
  • Experience in fintech, consumer financial services, or payments.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to distill complex financial and regulatory issues for diverse audiences.
  • Sound judgment on messaging and public positioning; comfort advising senior leadership.
  • Ability to work independently and manage competing priorities in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.
  • Willingness to travel nationally as needed.

  • Experience working with fintech or financial services trade associations.
  • Existing relationships with state financial regulators, state legislators, the CFPB, or other federal financial agencies.
  • Bachelor’s degree or higher in public policy, political science, or a related field.

🏥 Medical, dental, vision — Kikoff covers the full cost for employees, 50% for dependents

The Group Project Supervisor at BOLD is an expert in portfolio planning, operational leadership, prioritization, and cross-workstream delivery. They translate account priorities into an integrated delivery plan, creating forward visibility across timelines, dependencies, decisions, risks, and resource needs.

They are someone who can meticulously plan multiple concurrent workstreams while managing the impacts, risks, and dependencies between each project. Working in partnership with Client Services and functional leads, this person will connect client priorities and project requirements to a clear, achievable portfolio delivery plan. They will ensure that business decisions, timing implications, and operational trade-offs are visible early enough for the team and client to act.

As part of the Delivery team within the Project Management department, the Group Project Supervisor will manage the operational connection between project needs and client priorities. The role reports into BOLD Project Management for professional development, standards, and ways of working, while operating day to day as an embedded member of the client portfolio team.

The Group Project Supervisor will be responsible for the integrated portfolio plan for a specific client, with a primary focus on maintaining a consolidated view of all active and planned work. They will work closely with Client Services, Project Management, Scientific, Creative, Digital, Editorial, and other relevant teams to gather accurate inputs and identify priorities, decisions, risks, resource needs, and interdependencies as the portfolio evolves.

The Group Project Supervisor is the operational lead for the client portfolio. They do not replace Client Services account leadership, scientific strategy, or day-to-day ownership of individual deliverables. Instead, they connect these functions through an integrated portfolio plan, establish clear operating discipline, and ensure that risks, dependencies, resource needs, and decisions are surfaced and acted upon at the right time.

Working in close collaboration with the Client Services team, the Group Project Supervisor is a key integrated collaborator and requires experience working on projects that span strategy, scientific content, creative, and digital delivery.

As a developing role within BOLD, this position allows the Group Project Supervisor to help define and strengthen portfolio-level program management over time. This is an exciting opportunity for someone looking to demonstrate ownership and expertise while remaining open to change, collaboration, and growth.

DAY TO DAY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Operational ownership of the integrated portfolio plan for a specific client, in partnership with the Client Services account lead.
  • Maintain a consolidated, forward-looking view of the client portfolio, connecting individual project timelines to account priorities, review windows, stakeholder availability, and business-critical milestones.
  • Translate portfolio information into clear, decision-oriented reports and status updates that distinguish progress, risks, decisions required, and actions needed.
  • Identify decision points, dependencies, bottlenecks, and potential delivery conflicts early, clearly articulating the if/then implications of timeline or priority changes.
  • Provide structured recommendations on sequencing, prioritization, and mitigation when timelines, resources, or client priorities compete.
  • Demonstrate an understanding of the client’s needs and proactively identify practical solutions that support successful program delivery.
  • Produce and manage program status reports, integrated timelines, risk and decision logs, dependency maps, and capacity views.
  • Create visibility into upcoming activity so that resource needs, review requirements, and stakeholder decisions can be anticipated rather than managed reactively.
  • Facilitate regular portfolio-planning and prioritization discussions with Client Services, Scientific, Creative, Digital, Editorial, Finance, and other relevant functions.
  • Support client-facing conversations by framing risks and trade-offs constructively and bringing solutions and options rather than simply reporting issues.
  • Provide program-management expertise, clear delivery recommendations, and confident issue resolution in client-facing settings.
  • Partner with project leads and department leads to anticipate resource needs, identify capacity conflicts, and agree mitigation plans before delivery is affected.
  • Maintain awareness of approved scope, assumptions, and budget constraints so that delivery risks, changes, and potential out-of-scope implications are flagged promptly to Client Services.
  • Coordinate with partner agencies and Assembled Intelligence functions where workstreams overlap, clarifying dependencies, handoffs, ownership, and timing.
  • Identify and implement operational improvements that strengthen quality, efficiency, visibility, and collaboration across the client portfolio.

  • Ability to translate complex delivery information into concise recommendations for senior clients and agency leadership.
  • Experience facilitating prioritization and scenario-planning conversations where timelines, resources, and stakeholder needs compete.
  • Strong judgment in distinguishing between issues that can be resolved within the team and those requiring escalation or a client decision.
  • Experience working in a matrixed agency environment across Client Services, Scientific or Content, Creative, Digital, Editorial, Finance, and Production.

jobs.description:
Looma Background

Looma is an in-store digital media platform focused on storytelling, education, and recommendations. Their network of in-store screens helps retailers better modernize and monetize their stores, while enabling brands to tell their story directly at the point of decision. All content that airs on Looma’s network is produced or edited by Relay™, their global network of independent filmmakers, editors, and other creators who specialize in point-of-decision content.

Position Summary

Looma is growing fast. We’re adding new national retailers and expanding with existing partners, and every new program means hundreds or thousands of stores, multiple hardware and install vendors, and a retailer team counting on us to launch on time. The Senior Implementation Manager will own these deployments end to end.

This is a senior, hands-on role. You’ll independently run our largest and most complex rollouts with our most important partners. You won’t just track the plan; you’ll write the playbooks, solve the problems blocking the work, and be the person retailers and vendors trust to get it done. You’ll also own project management as a discipline at Looma, building the program, documentation, and training that let the rest of the team deliver at the same level.

The responsibilities for this role can be split into three primary categories:

  1. Deployment leadership | 50%
  2. Hands-on problem solving & partner management | 25%
  3. Building Looma’s project management practice | 25%

Deployment leadership (50%)

  • Own large, multi-site retail deployments end to end, from planning and procurement through install, launch, and handoff to steady-state operations
  • Build and maintain integrated project plans spanning hardware procurement, certification, site surveys, installation, device registration, content readiness, and go-live
  • Coordinate cross-functional work across Retail Ops, Product & Tech, Sales, and Content, as well as with partners and vendors, so every launch is ready on every front
  • Track progress against milestones, surface risks early, and drive decisions to keep deployments on schedule
  • Maintain a single source of truth and report clear, concise status to Looma leadership and retail partners

Hands-on problem solving & partner management (25%)

  • Roll up your sleeves to clear blockers directly, whether that means troubleshooting an install issue, reworking a timeline, or chasing down a missing approval
  • Produce the artifacts a deployment needs: Install guides, store communications, rollout schedules, trackers, and launch readiness checklists
  • Serve as a primary point of contact for retailer stakeholders, from store operations and IT to merchandising and corporate leadership
  • Manage install, hardware, and logistics vendors, holding them accountable to quality, cost, and timeline
  • Travel to stores, retailer offices, and vendor sites (~25%) to oversee pilots, resolve issues in the field, and build relationships
  • Capture lessons from every deployment and turn them into improvements for the next one

Building Looma’s project management practice (25%)

  • Own project management as a discipline at Looma, defining the standards, tools, and rituals our deployments run on
  • Create repeatable playbooks and templates for new-retailer launches, expansions, and hardware refreshes
  • Own project management documentation and training, and keep both current as we scale
  • Mentor and coach more junior project and implementation team members
  • Partner with Retail Ops leadership to improve planning, resourcing, and forecasting across the deployment portfolio

Experience

  • 7+ years of project, program, or implementation management experience, including ownership of large, complex deployments
  • Track record of leading multi-site physical rollouts (e.g. hardware, fixtures, or technology installed across hundreds of locations), including managing field and install vendors
  • Experience working directly with large retail chains or in retail technology / in-store media strongly preferred
  • Experience creating project management processes, documentation, or training for a team
  • Comfort with project management tools (e.g. Asana) and spreadsheets for planning and tracking

Attributes

  • Owner’s mindset | You take full responsibility for outcomes and don’t wait for permission to solve problems
  • Calm under pressure | You stay organized and decisive when timelines slip or plans change
  • Clear communicator | You write and present crisply to audiences from store associates to retailer executives
  • Builder | You enjoy creating structure where little exists and leaving processes better than you found them
  • Generous teacher | You make the people around you better and take pride in their growth
  • Detail-oriented | Nothing slips through the cracks
  • Willing to travel approximately 25% of the time

Structure & Compensation

Looma will provide a competitive compensation package consisting of base salary and stock options. All Looma compensation packages include some cash / equity flexibility (i.e. you can opt for more equity and less cash or vice-versa).

Benefits

  • Employee coverage for health, dental, and vision (gold plan)
  • Unlimited PTO (3-week minimum)
  • Flexible office setting (office, flex, or WFH, with associated stipends)
  • Craftsmanship stipend
  • Paid parental leave
  • 401(k) plan

Our Values

At Looma, we strive to be and/or create work that is:

  • For You | Generous, generative, humble, in your corner
  • Incisive | Pragmatic, wise, perceptive, insightful
  • Beautiful & Clear | Polished, elegant, detailed, conveys a sense of craftsmanship
  • Undaunted | Tenacious, courageous, indomitable, “impenetrable ray of sun”
  • Dependable | Trustworthy, reliable, nothing slips through the cracks

Diversity & Nondiscrimination

Looma is committed to promoting diversity both in our workplace and through the stories we tell. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability status, age, marital status, protected veteran status, class or caste status, or any other protected class. Our global nondiscrimination policy covers these protected classes in every market in which we do business.

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis.

jobs.title: VP of Research, Machine Learning
jobs.excerpt: Our client is an AI-native product company built to replace how billions of people manage their digital lives — starting with email, notes, and task tools that were never designed to be AI-native.
jobs.description:
Our client is an AI-native product company built to replace how billions of people manage their digital lives — starting with email, notes, and task tools that were never designed to be AI-native. It's backed by multi-million-dollar investment and built remote-first from day one, with a clear target: cut the time it takes users to get everyday things done by roughly 90%. That means solving the problems most AI products avoid — long-running workflows, persistent context, and reliable behavior under real-world, non-deterministic conditions. The team is small and high-talent-density by design, not by necessity, and moves at a pace that matches the scale of what it's building.

About the Role

You'll own the research and intelligence direction of this system — defining how the AI reasons, evaluates, and improves in a product used with high frequency.

What You'll Do

  • Set and evolve the research direction for the company's core intelligence, including context representation, memory, reasoning, planning, and orchestration

  • Decide when to design new model architectures versus adapting or leveraging frontier open-source or commercial models

  • Define evaluation frameworks that measure real-world usefulness, robustness, safety, and long-term behavior — not benchmark vanity

  • Own alignment, safety, and guardrail strategy as first-class product concerns

  • Guide exploration of frontier techniques: retrieval-augmented training, mixture-of-experts, distillation, multi-agent orchestration, multimodal systems

  • Shape early product intelligence direction in close partnership with product and application engineering

  • Set the technical bar for research rigor, judgment, and taste across the organization

Requirements

  • Deep experience building or evolving real machine learning systems used in production

  • Strong technical judgment around model behavior, failure modes, and long-horizon trade-offs

  • A builder's mindset — you care about systems that work in the real world, not just ideas

  • Comfortable making irreversible or high-impact decisions with incomplete information

  • An obsession with evaluation, correctness, and how systems behave over time

  • High ownership mentality — you operate as a founder, not a manager

This probably isn't a fit if your focus is primarily publishing, incremental benchmarks, or managing a large research organization — this role is not that.

Tech Stack

Python · PyTorch / JAX · GPU-based training and inference systems

What to Expect

The best products in the world are built by small, world-class teams. Decisions are made collectively, at rapid speed — balancing high-quality shipping with fast learning. You'll be expected to bring structure, exercise judgment, and execute independently.

Compensation and benefits are competitive and vary by location; the package includes base salary and equity, discussed openly with you as part of the process.

If there's a fit, expect 3–4 interviews total, followed by a prompt, transparent decision.

jobs.excerpt: Staff Data Platform EngineerLocation: NYC HQ or Remote (U.
jobs.description:
Staff Data Platform Engineer

Location: NYC HQ or Remote (U.S.)| Full-time | Engineering

Who we are.

Reality Defender is an award-winning cybersecurity company helping enterprises and governments detect deepfakes and AI-generated media. Utilizing a patented multi-model approach, Reality Defender is robust against the bleeding edge of generative platforms producing video, audio, imagery, and text media. Reality Defender's API-first deepfake detection platform empowers teams and developers alike to identify fraud, disinformation campaigns, and harmful deepfakes in real time.

Backed by world class investors including DCVC, Illuminate Financial, Y Combinator, Booz Allen Hamilton, IBM, Accenture, Rackhouse, and Argon VC, Reality Defender works with leading enterprise clients, financial institutions, and governments in order to ensure AI-generated media is not used for malicious purposes.

Youtube: Reality Defender Wins RSA Most Innovative Startup

The Staff Data Platform Engineer Role.

Reality Defender's detection models are only as strong as the data behind them, and every new generative tool raises the bar on the volume and variety of media we need to train and evaluate against. The Staff Data Platform Engineer will own the shared AI data platform behind our vision, audio, and multimodal research, turning acquired and internally generated image, video, audio, and text data into reliable, reproducible datasets, from continuous ingestion through processing, governance, and export. This is a senior, hands-on role where you'll complete our Databricks and distributed processing platform and build the reusable infrastructure behind our in-house synthetic data generation, including producing the very deepfakes our models learn to catch. This is a full-time role, reporting to our Director of Data. Responsibilities include:

  • Own the end-to-end data platform for AI research: continuous ingestion, preprocessing, governance, and export of image, video, audio, and text data at high volume.

  • Complete and scale our Databricks lakehouse and distributed processing stack (Spark, Ray, or similar), making architecture and build-vs-buy decisions that hold up as data volume grows.

  • Build reusable infrastructure for in-house synthetic data generation, so researchers can produce new deepfake variants across modalities on demand instead of one-off.

  • Make every dataset reproducible and traceable through versioning, lineage, metadata, quality checks, and stable train/eval splits, so any model result can be tied back to the exact data behind it.

  • Own pipeline reliability, observability, and processing cost per dataset as core metrics of the platform.

  • Partner with ML researchers to understand their data needs and turn them into self-serve tools that speed up model iteration.

  • Mentor engineers and raise the bar on data engineering practices: code review, testing, documentation, and runbooks.

  • Work with Security and compliance stakeholders to make sure data handling, licensing, and access controls meet the standards our enterprise and government clients expect.

  • Help shape the long-term data platform roadmap with engineering and research leadership.

Who you are.

  • 8+ years building data platforms or data infrastructure, including staff- or lead-level ownership of production pipelines that generate, ingest, or deliver data at high volume.

  • Deep hands-on experience with distributed processing (Spark, Ray, or similar) and lakehouse platforms, ideally Databricks, on top of cloud object storage (S3, GCS, or Azure Blob).

  • Production experience with Databricks, Unity Catalog, Delta Lake, and Spark on AWS, including performance tuning, access controls, and operational troubleshooting.

  • Experience working with large unstructured media such as video, audio, or images, including the realities of large files, decoding and transcoding, and metadata at scale.

jobs.excerpt: About UsAt Memora, we’re digitizing one of the oldest and most overlooked categories on earth: the cemetery.
jobs.description:
About Us

At Memora, we’re digitizing one of the oldest and most overlooked categories on earth: the cemetery. Most still run on paper maps, spreadsheets, and institutional memory. We are replacing this with an ecosystem for everyone who touches a cemetery: the leadership running it, the field teams maintaining it, the families visiting it, and the local partners serving them.

We’re backed by leading investors and guided by a team of experienced founders and engineers from well known tech names reimagining a category long overdue for change. We’re deliberately lean, and will keep it that way.

Job Description

This is a remote position.

Product Lead – Memora

We’re hiring a Product Lead to own the product end to end: a hands-on IC role with real product and cultural ownership. You are not a backlog administrator. You are the person who decides what we build, why, and in what order — and who stands behind that call.

The Why

Memora is growing rapidly. We’re selling into a sector with almost no digital precedent, which means there is no playbook to copy and no competitor roadmap to trail. We need someone who can:

  • Get the truth from the field — cemetery leaders, gardeners, and grieving families — rather than from a meeting room
  • Turn messy sector reality (Danish folkekirke structures, legacy systems, public-sector procurement) into product decisions engineers can build from
  • Prioritise ruthlessly across three live surfaces and say no with reasons
  • Be a thoughtful, methodical product voice in a small team where every person has outsized influence

The Surfaces

  • Tooling — Jira + Confluence, Figma, PostHog, Grafana for the operational picture

Who you are

Must have:

  • Typically 6+ years in product, including at least one role at a growth startup or as an early product hire
  • A track record of shipping software people actually use — you can point at outcomes, not roadmaps
  • Genuinely comfortable doing fieldwork: you will stand on cemeteries in the rain and learn more there than anywhere else. Talk with our customers, cemetery leaders, gardeners. Break down the data sources, organise product summits with our userbase.
  • Strong written communication — you can make a complex trade-off legible in a page, and you write your own specs
  • Technical enough to hold a real conversation about trade-offs with engineers, and to read the data yourself
  • Comfortable operating in a small team without a clear playbook: you can scope your own work, write your own docs, and chase your own answers

Strongly preferred:

  • B2B/B2G SaaS experience: sales cycles, real customer relationships, public-sector quirks
  • Operations-heavy or field-workforce products, where the software has to survive contact with a real working day
  • Experience with compliance-sensitive data (we’re GDPR + public-sector)
  • Marketplace or two-sided product experience

Bonus:

  • Experience with cemetery, GIS, or public records systems
  • You have run discovery in a sector that had never been sold software before
  • Fluent in Danish

How we work

We’re building Memora to be the kind of company we’d want to work for ourselves: high trust, low bureaucracy, and full of people who care deeply about doing great work.

  • We’re remote by design. No, we don’t track hours or expect people to be online all day, but we do expect ownership, communication, and roughly 4 hours of overlap with Copenhagen (CET).
  • We believe great work and great lives aren’t in competition with each other. Remote work means your whole life doesn’t stop when work starts and that’s a good thing by us. Families, school pickups, deep-focus afternoons: we welcome the whole human. We optimize for people doing the best work of their careers while still having a life they’re excited to live.
  • We’re a small team, which means you’ll have real autonomy and real influence. Everyone talks to customers, helps onboard them, visits cemeteries, and sees first-hand how their work impacts real people. There are no layers of management and no “that’s someone else’s problem” mentality.
  • We’re low ego and high standards. We challenge ideas, admit mistakes, ask questions, and care more about getting to the right answer than being right. Psychological safety matters here, and so does excellence.
  • We’re async-first and intentionally lightweight. We write things down, keep meetings purposeful, and avoid process for process’ sake. Our default approach is simple: communicate clearly, make good decisions, and ship.
  • And because we’re building a real team, not just a collection of Slack profiles, we get together for an offsite three times a year somewhere in the world. Last time, we spent the week skiing and working together, because the best ideas don’t always happen in a meeting room.

Compensation & equity

  • Senior salary (currency calibrated to location)
  • Meaningful early-employee warrant grant: we’re early enough that this matters and we want you for the full journey
  • Annual leave + Danish-equivalent benefits
  • 3 offsites a year

jobs.description:
Financial Leadership Partner (CFO Level Consultant)
The Herring Group | Remote | TX or GA | 30 to 35 hours/week during business hours

Most people will not read this thoroughly or will think it is too good to be true.

What we believe

The Herring Group is a professional services and data analytics firm. We work with owners of landscape companies who have built something real and want to keep it without being crushed by it.

We optimize two margins, not one.

  • Profit margin. We put our clients on a disciplined Path to 12% profitability. Most landscape businesses run at 3 to 7%. The solution is not a mystery; it is a system. We build the system.
  • Life margin. If the owner cannot take a three-week vacation without the business wobbling, we have not done our job. Profit that requires the owner's presence to operate is not profit. It is a salary with extra steps.

These margins are not separate goals. They reinforce each other. A business that cannot give its owner a life cannot give its employees one either, and neither carries 12% for long.

Autonomy and accountability. We help our clients build teams that think, decide, and own outcomes.

What you would actually do

  • Hold a portfolio of SMB clients (companies with $3M to $50M in revenue) as their outsourced financial leader. Own the models, forecasts, dashboards, and KPIs that leadership actually uses, not the ones that live in a forgotten folder. Help owners and management teams every month translate numbers into decisions.
  • Push them on pricing they have been afraid to raise, labor efficiency they have been afraid to measure, and margin they did not know was leaking.
  • Help us get sharper, too. Every client’s engagement is a chance to improve our methodology, our delivery, and our tools so the next client benefits from everything we have learned on this one.

Who this is for

  • You have done this work for 10 to 20 years, with titles like CFO, Controller, FP&A Director, Principal Consultant, or Business Owner. You have worked inside SMBs, not just for them. You know what the owner is actually worried about at 5:47 a.m.
  • You can build a model in your sleep, but models are not what you are most proud of. You are proud of a conversation that changed a decision that changed a company.
  • You think like a business owner. You have previously owned a business and want back in the game without all the responsibility that comes with it.
  • You do not need everything to be handed to you on a silver platter and you do not mind getting in the weeds if there is a purpose for it.
  • You have thick skin in a professional sense. Clients hire us to tell them what they need to hear, not what they want to hear.
  • You find 30 to 35 focused hours a week more appealing than 50 unfocused ones, and you would rather be paid for results than seat time.
  • You want work that is meaningful, interesting, and challenging with a high degree of autonomy.

Who does not fit

  • Anyone who wants a W-2 with a ladder to climb. We measure personal success by client success.
  • Anyone who wants to build the model and hand it off. We stay in the room.
  • Anyone who thinks "mission-driven" is marketing copy. We believe it.
  • Anyone who wants an assistant to do all the work. We roll up our sleeves and do what it takes.

The facts

  • Location. Fully remote. Must reside in Texas or Georgia.
  • Commitment. Minimum 30 hours per week, during business hours.
  • Reality. You will manage multiple client engagements at once in a fast-paced consulting environment. Success in this role requires resilience, sound judgment, personal accountability, and the ability to make progress without constant supervision. We will not pretend otherwise.
  • Clients. We provide them.
  • Compensation. Competitive hourly pay with a pay-for-performance component.

Benefits. Health insurance, PTO, vacation, and a Simple IRA match.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in finance, Accounting, or Economics or an MBA required.
  • Minimum 10 years of experience in financial leadership, with titles such as CFO, Controller, FP&A Director, or Business Owner.
  • Hands-on experience supporting small to mid-sized businesses ($3M to $100M+ in annual revenue).
  • Proven ability to drive profitability improvement, margin expansion, and cash flow optimization through financial analysis.
  • Advanced proficiency in financial modeling, dashboards, and analytics tools.
  • Exceptional communication, presentation, and relationship-building skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple client engagements concurrently in a fast-paced consulting environment.
  • Previous business owner or entrepreneurial experience considered a strong plus.
  • Must reside in Texas or Georgia.

Benefits

Health insurance, PTO, vacation, and a Simple IRA match.

Salary: We offer highly competitive salaries along with a robust bonus and benefits package. Compensation figures displayed on external sites do not accurately reflect our comprehensive total compensation for our Financial Leadership Partners.

Blue Star Families is the largest nonprofit dedicated to making military life better for families. Each year, we support over 1.5 million military- and veteran-connected family members through a national network of 300,000+ members and local chapters in communities across the country.

Our mission is simple and bold: We make military life awesome for families. We listen, share, partner, and act to deliver evidence-based, data-driven solutions that work for real people. jobs.description:
Strategia, Zgodność i Zarządzanie (Governance & Compliance)

Współpraca z Dyrekcją przy budowaniu kultury i strategii bezpieczeństwa oraz adaptacji standardów korporacyjnych, w tym frameworku NIST.

Zapewnienie zgodności organizacji z kluczowymi regulacjami rynkowymi i europejskimi (m.in. NIS2, CRA, RODO).

Opracowywanie polityk bezpieczeństwa, definiowanie i raportowanie wskaźników KPI do Zarządu oraz facylitacja komitetów sterujących ds. bezpieczeństwa.

Zarządzanie Ryzykiem i Architektura (Security by Design)

Opracowywanie i bieżąca aktualizacja mapy ryzyk cybernetycznych oraz realizacja adekwatnych mechanizmów kontrolnych (Kontrola N2).

Eksperckie wsparcie działu projektowego gwarantujące integrację wymagań bezpieczeństwa od wczesnych faz koncepcyjnych (Security by Design), w tym weryfikacja architektury i nadzór nad zlecanymi testami penetracyjnymi.

Operacje i Zabezpieczenia Techniczne (SecOps & Protection)

Projektowanie, wdrażanie oraz utrzymywanie platform zabezpieczających infrastrukturę, w szczególności rozwiązań klasy EDR/XDR, mechanizmów uwierzytelniania wieloskładnikowego (MFA) oraz firewalli.

Ciągła weryfikacja efektywności zabezpieczeń w ramach całej floty urządzeń (serwery, stacje robocze, urządzenia mobilne, aplikacje).

Kompleksowa realizacja procesu Vulnerability Management – od detekcji podatności, przez rekomendacje mitygacyjne, po nadzór nad wdrożeniem poprawek we współpracy z działem IT.

Monitorowanie i Reagowanie na Incydenty (Detection & Incident Response)

Analiza alertów z systemów bezpieczeństwa oraz koordynacja działań zewnętrznego centrum operacyjnego (SOC) w celu zapewnienia ciągłości monitoringu w trybie HNO (obsługa i reagowanie poza standardowymi godzinami pracy).

Kompleksowe zarządzanie incydentami bezpieczeństwa: identyfikacja, mitygacja zagrożeń oraz opracowywanie działań naprawczych w ramach procedury RETEX (analiza poakcyjna typu lessons learned).

Optymalizacja procedur reagowania na incydenty oraz projektowanie i koordynacja cyklicznych ćwiczeń kryzysowych.

Budowanie Świadomości (Awareness)

Kształtowanie świadomości zagrożeń poprzez realizację rocznych planów szkoleniowych dla całej organizacji, w tym koordynację symulacji phishingowych oraz modułów e-learningowych.

Transfer wiedzy i prowadzenie specjalistycznych warsztatów podnoszących kompetencje z zakresu bezpieczeństwa dla zespołów IT

Realizacja powyższych obszarów ma na celu zbudowanie proaktywnego modelu ochrony organizacji, minimalizację ryzyka cybernetycznego oraz zagwarantowanie najwyższych standardów bezpieczeństwa, adekwatnych do surowych wymogów regulacyjnych i operacyjnych. Rola stanowi centralny punkt kompetencyjny, łączący architekturę bezpieczeństwa z bieżącym reagowaniem na ewoluujące zagrożenia.

jobs.excerpt: Role ScopeOwns data architecture across multiple domains, with dual focus: (1) modernizing legacy database systems—particularly large-scale SQL Server environments with complex stored procedures containing embedded business logic, and (2) designing AI-native data infrastructure—semantic data models, vector databases, and RAG architectures that power AI agents and workflows.
jobs.description:
Role Scope

Owns data architecture across multiple domains, with dual focus: (1) modernizing legacy database systems—particularly large-scale SQL Server environments with complex stored procedures containing embedded business logic, and (2) designing AI-native data infrastructure—semantic data models, vector databases, and RAG architectures that power AI agents and workflows. Establishes patterns for domain-driven data models, event-driven data flows, and canonical schemas across relational, NoSQL, analytical, and AI-optimized data platforms.

The Problem We're Solving

We have two interconnected data architecture challenges.

Legacy modernization: SQL Server stored procedures that have grown to thousands of lines, with business logic deeply embedded in T-SQL that should live in application services. These procedures are difficult to test, impossible to reuse, and create tight coupling between business rules and data access. They slow down development, complicate domain ownership, and resist modernization efforts.

AI data infrastructure: We're building AI agents and agentic workflows that require purpose-built data architecture—semantic models that capture domain knowledge, vector databases for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), embedding pipelines, and knowledge graphs that give AI systems the context they need to operate effectively. This isn't about bolting AI onto existing data systems; it's about designing data infrastructure that makes AI-native applications possible.

These challenges intersect: the domain knowledge locked in legacy systems becomes training data and context for AI agents. The canonical models we build for modernization become the semantic foundation for AI retrieval. We need database architects who can work across both dimensions—modernizing legacy while building for an AI-native future.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a Senior Database Architect who combines deep expertise in legacy database systems with forward-looking vision for AI-native data architecture. You'll lead the decomposition of complex stored procedures while simultaneously designing the vector databases, embedding strategies, and semantic models that power our AI agents and workflows.

This is an AI-first role in two senses: you'll leverage AI to accelerate your own work (stored procedure analysis, migration generation, schema documentation), and you'll design the data infrastructure that AI systems depend on. If you're excited about both solving hard legacy database problems and architecting the data layer for AI-native applications, this role is for you.

What You'll Do

Legacy Database Modernization

  • Analyze and decompose large SQL Server stored procedures (1,000+ lines) with embedded business logic, creating migration strategies that extract logic into domain services

  • Design patterns for separating business rules from data access, enabling stored procedures to become thin data-access layers while business logic moves to application services

  • Lead refactoring efforts that align database structures with domain-driven design: bounded contexts, aggregates, and domain events

  • Implement event-driven patterns that decouple systems from direct database dependencies: change data capture, outbox patterns, event sourcing where appropriate

  • Optimize query performance, indexing strategies, and execution plans as part of modernization efforts

  • Create migration playbooks and tooling that engineering teams can apply to their own stored procedure modernization

AI Data Infrastructure & Semantic Modeling

  • Design semantic data models that capture domain knowledge in structures optimized for AI retrieval and reasoning

  • Architect vector database solutions for RAG implementations: embedding strategies, chunking approaches, similarity search optimization, and hybrid retrieval patterns

  • Design and implement embedding pipelines that transform domain content into vector representations suitable for AI agent consumption

  • Establish knowledge graph patterns where appropriate: entity relationships, ontologies, and graph-based retrieval for complex domain reasoning

  • Define data architectures for AI agent context: what data agents need, how it's structured, how freshness and consistency are maintained

  • Design evaluation frameworks for RAG quality: retrieval accuracy, relevance scoring, and feedback loops for continuous improvement

Modern Data Platform Architecture

  • Design canonical data models and schemas that are flexible, extensible, and aligned with business domain concepts

  • Architect data solutions across multiple platforms: SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MongoDB/Cosmos DB, Snowflake, and vector databases (Pinecone, Weaviate, pgvector, Azure AI Search)

  • Design event-driven data flows: Kafka-based event streaming, materialized views, CQRS patterns, and real-time data synchronization

  • Establish data platform infrastructure patterns: data pipelines, ETL/ELT orchestration, data quality frameworks, and observability

  • Define data residency, partitioning, and multi-region strategies for performance and compliance

  • Create reference architectures for common data patterns that domain teams can adopt

AI-First Database Engineering

  • Leverage AI coding assistants (GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code) to accelerate stored procedure analysis, refactoring, and migration

  • Build AI-powered tools for database engineering: automated stored procedure analysis, schema documentation generators, migration assistants, and query optimization recommenders

  • Create AI-consumable artifacts: structured documentation, annotated schemas, and context files that enable AI agents to understand and work with database systems

  • Author database architecture skills that encode patterns, constraints, and best practices for AI-assisted development

  • Develop prompts, workflows, and tooling that help engineering teams apply AI effectively to database modernization tasks

Cross-Domain Leadership

  • Partner with AI/ML teams to ensure data architecture supports agent and workflow requirements

  • Collaborate with domain teams to understand their data requirements and design solutions aligned with domain ownership

  • Work with application architects to ensure data architecture supports service-oriented and event-driven designs

  • Contribute to Enterprise Architecture Council (EAC) standards for data architecture, modeling conventions, and technology selection

  • Mentor engineers on database design, optimization, semantic modeling, and AI data infrastructure

What You'll Bring

Required Experience

  • 8–12 years in database engineering and architecture, with significant experience in enterprise-scale SQL Server environments

  • Deep SQL Server expertise: T-SQL optimization, stored procedure design and refactoring, query plan analysis, indexing strategies, and performance tuning

  • Hands-on modernization experience: track record of decomposing complex stored procedures and migrating business logic to application services

  • Multi-platform data architecture: experience designing solutions across relational (SQL Server, PostgreSQL), NoSQL (MongoDB, Cosmos DB), and analytical (Snowflake, data lakehouse) platforms

  • Event-driven data patterns: CDC, Kafka, outbox pattern, event sourcing, CQRS—practical experience implementing these in production

  • Data modeling expertise: canonical models, dimensional modeling, schema evolution, and designing for extensibility

AI & Semantic Data Competencies

  • Vector database experience: hands-on with at least one vector DB (Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus, pgvector, Azure AI Search, or similar)

  • RAG architecture understanding: embedding models, chunking strategies, retrieval optimization, hybrid search, and reranking patterns

  • Semantic modeling: experience designing data structures optimized for AI retrieval—knowledge representation, ontologies, or domain-specific schemas for AI consumption

  • Understanding of embedding pipelines: text preprocessing, embedding generation, vector indexing, and incremental updates

  • Familiarity with LLM context requirements: what data AI agents need, token constraints, context window optimization

AI-Native Engineering Practices

  • 2+ years actively using AI coding assistants for database work; deep understanding of how to prompt effectively for SQL and data engineering tasks

  • Experience building tools, scripts, or automation that leverage AI/LLM capabilities

  • Familiarity with structured artifact creation for AI consumption: documented schemas, annotated procedures, context files

  • Vision for AI-assisted database engineering and ability to build tooling that enables it

Technical Depth

  • Strong programming skills in at least one backend language (C#, Java, Python) for building migration tooling, embedding pipelines, and services

  • Cloud data services experience: Azure SQL, Cosmos DB, Azure AI Search, Azure Synapse, Snowflake, or AWS equivalents

  • Infrastructure-as-code for data platforms: Terraform, ARM/Bicep, or CloudFormation

  • Understanding of domain-driven design and how data architecture supports bounded contexts

  • Familiarity with data governance, lineage, and compliance requirements (HIPAA, PCI-DSS)

Preferred Experience

  • Background in healthcare, benefits, payments, or similarly regulated industries

  • Experience building RAG systems or AI-powered search/retrieval applications

  • Knowledge graph experience: Neo4j, Amazon Neptune, or similar graph databases

  • Contributions to database tooling, AI/ML data infrastructure, or open-source projects

  • Experience mentoring engineers or leading database/data architecture communities of practice

What Success Looks Like

In 90 days: Completed assessment of priority stored procedure modernization targets and AI data infrastructure needs; delivered first AI-assisted analysis tooling; established vector database patterns for initial RAG implementations

In 6 months: Led decomposition of at least one major stored procedure system; semantic data models and RAG architecture patterns established and being adopted; AI-powered database engineering tools in active use by teams

In 12 months: Measurable reduction in stored procedure complexity across priority systems; AI data infrastructure supporting production agent workflows; recognized as the go-to expert for both database modernization and AI-native data architecture

Why This Role Matters

Data architecture is being transformed from two directions simultaneously.

From the legacy side: business logic buried in stored procedures creates invisible dependencies that resist refactoring. Traditional approaches to database modernization are slow, manual, and error-prone—but AI can analyze thousands of lines of T-SQL, identify patterns, and accelerate migrations in ways that weren't possible before.

From the AI side: agents and workflows need purpose-built data infrastructure. The semantic models, vector databases, and knowledge representations you design will determine how effectively AI can reason about our domains. This isn't a nice-to-have capability; it's foundational to our AI-native engineering strategy.

You'll work at the intersection of these transformations—solving hard legacy problems while building the data infrastructure that makes AI-native applications possible. The patterns you establish will shape how we approach data architecture across the enterprise.

Position: Data Architect Reports to: Director, Data Intelligence Position Term: Full Time Permanent Primary Location: Mississauga, Ontario, Canada Workplace Type: Remote (Within Canada)

Job Purpose

The Data Architect is responsible for the design, governance and integrity of World Vision Canada's data architecture. The role defines how data is structured, stored, integrated and made available for reporting, analytics and artificial intelligence, and translates business information requirements into a well-governed and reusable data foundation. It ensures that data is managed as an enterprise asset that is consistent across systems, reliable for decision-making, and able to support the organization as its technology environment changes, thereby supporting the organization's mission.

Reporting to the Director, Data Intelligence, the incumbent develops the organization's data architecture framework and principles for the Director's approval and is thereafter accountable for their application across the enterprise. The incumbent owns the data architecture for the multi-year transformation program and sets the multi-year direction and roadmap for the organization's data architecture and platform. Support for day-to-day operations is provided on an as-available basis and is ad-hoc in nature. This is a hands-on role, with results achieved through modernizing data flows, publishing standards, documentation and design reviews.

Responsibilities

  • Designs the enterprise data architecture. Develops the conceptual, logical and physical data architecture, including the data platform, canonical data models, and the standards that govern how data is structured, stored and moved. Establishes the framework and principles that govern this work and holds all designs, internal and vendor, to them.
  • Develops and presents the data architecture for senior leadership approval. Prepares and presents the data architecture, its roadmap and material design decisions to senior leadership for approval, frames the options and the trade-offs between them, and sets the multi-year direction for the organization's data architecture and platform.
  • Defines data integration and interoperability standards. Establishes the contract-first patterns, interfaces and reusable standards by which systems exchange data, including schema and interface contracts defined in advance of build. This includes the standards for secure data-sharing with federated partner organizations across the wider World Vision partnership, distinct from the organization's own enterprise data governance which the role helps uphold. Sets the data architecture requirements that solution designs must satisfy, rules on data design questions arising within solution architecture, and confirms that individual solutions stay coherent with the wider data architecture.
  • Architects governed, reusable data products. Designs trustworthy, well-defined data products and master data structures, including consolidated master records and analytical models, that support reporting, analytics and machine learning. Ensures these are documented, discoverable and reusable across business areas rather than rebuilt for each initiative.
  • Establishes data quality, master data and lifecycle standards. Defines the controls for data quality, master data management, retention and remediation, and requires delivery teams to apply them in day-to-day practice. Sets quality and design standards at a level sufficient for data to be consumed reliably by analytics and artificial intelligence, including requirements for completeness, consistency, labelling and documented meaning. Monitors adherence, directs the remediation of data quality and data definition issues at source, and withholds acceptance where the controls are not met.
  • Sets standards for AI and machine learning data use and platform portability. Defines how analytical and machine learning workloads consume governed data, and designs for platform portability so that the organization avoids undue dependence on any single vendor or platform.
  • Establishes data security and protection standards. Defines how data is classified, protected and accessed, with particular attention to sensitive information and to data relating to donors, employees, and vulnerable populations, including children participating in the organization's programs. Ensures protection, privacy and access controls are included in designs from the outset, and that designs meet or exceed regulatory and organizational obligations.
  • Produces and maintains architecture documentation. Produces and maintains data architecture documentation, including conceptual, logical and physical data models, current and target state reference architectures, data flow and integration diagrams, architecture decision records and standards documentation. Maintains these as the reference used by delivery teams and as the record of architecture governance.
  • Governs solution and vendor designs through to delivery. Reviews solution and vendor designs against data architecture standards, prepares and reviews architecture decision records, and confirms alignment before designs proceed. Guides delivery teams through implementation, holds delivered systems to the architecture, and adjusts the architecture where implementation shows it to be wrong.

Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
  • Enterprise-architecture or cloud data-platform certification, for example TOGAF or a recognized cloud data credential. Preferred.

Experience

  • Ten or more years working in data management disciplines such as data modelling, data engineering or data science.
  • Five or more years in data architecture, including the design of lakehouse or warehouse-native patterns and of batch and streaming data flows in Snowflake and other cloud data platforms.
  • Demonstrated accountability for an enterprise data architecture, including setting standards adopted across delivery teams and vendors, and presenting architecture direction to senior leadership for approval.
  • Demonstrated delivery of master-data and golden-record solutions, and of governed, reusable data products, as well as warehouse-native customer data platforms.
  • Demonstrated experience setting data design direction for solution architects and delivery partners within an established technology or architecture function.
  • Experience designing data protection, classification and access controls for sensitive data.
  • Experience in a nonprofit or mission-driven organization. Preferred.

Technical skills

  • Defining data and application-programming-interface contracts in advance of build, including the use of schema registries and contract testing.
  • Advanced data modelling across conceptual, logical and physical layers, relational and dimensional, and strong SQL.
  • Familiarity with modern transformation frameworks, for example dbt, ELT patterns, and orchestration tooling, sufficient to define standards and review implementations.
  • Familiarity with Python or similar scripting languages for prototyping and automation.
  • Understanding of continuous integration and delivery and automated testing practices for data, including contract and schema testing, sufficient to embed them in standards and review vendor delivery against them.
  • Command of modern data architecture paradigms, including data mesh, data fabric and lakehouse, sufficient to select between them and defend the choice.
  • Familiarity with data catalog and metadata management tooling.
  • Proficiency with architecture modelling notations and tooling for producing models and diagrams, for example ArchiMate or UML.
  • Experience working in environments using Enterprise Agile frameworks.

Soft skills and competencies

  • Communicates clearly with both technical specialists and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Builds agreement on design direction across technical and business teams.
  • Applies sound judgement to complex and ambiguous design problems, balancing long-term architectural integrity against near-term delivery needs.
  • Records design decisions, applies standards consistently, and supports recommendations with evidence.

Why Consider Us?

  • Our competitive compensation & benefits include:
  • Health Spending Account
  • Up to 6% matched pension contributions
  • Parental leave top-up
  • Generous paid vacation, sick days, wellness and personal days
  • Office closed extra days before long weekends (6x/year)

  • We are Canada’s largest development, relief, and advocacy non-profit organization.
